definition_zh: 偏离常规；反常；一时的失常；测量偏差；光学像差；光行差；生物畸变；离群值
definition_en: a departure from what is usual or expected, and in science a systematic deviation in an image, a measurement, or a living form
core_image: 一条笔直的白色轨迹，在某个点忽然向外拐出一道弧，留下一小段偏斜的线。
scene: The committee treated the violent outburst as a momentary aberration rather than a sign of character.
sceneCN: 这里 aberration 是「一时的行为失常」（第 2 个义项）；句意：委员会把那次暴怒发作看作一时失常，而非性格的征兆。场景：会议室、被打断的发言、有人低头把这个词记进纪要。

senses.title: A departure from the usual course
senses.titleCN: 偏离常轨：从该走的线上滑开
senses.definition: a single departure from what is normal, expected, or standard, usually treated as an exception rather than a rule
senses.definitionCN: 一次偏离正常、预期或标准的情况，通常被当作例外而非常态
senses.example: Any aberration in the machine's rhythm was logged by the night technician.
senses.exampleCN: 机器节奏上任何一点偏离，都会被夜班技师记录下来。
senses.why: Latin aberrare is to wander off a path. The word keeps that picture: something has left the line it was supposed to follow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aberrare 就是“从路上走开”。这个词保留了那幅画面：某样东西离开了它本该跟随的线。

senses.title: A lapse in behaviour or judgement
senses.titleCN: 一时失常：脑子短暂离开常轨
senses.definition: a temporary failure of judgement or behaviour that is out of character for the person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一时判断或行为失控，与其平常性格不符
senses.example: In a moment of aberration he agreed to sign the false report.
senses.exampleCN: 在一时糊涂中，他同意签署那份虚假报告。
senses.why: The moral use grows from the spatial one: a mind that wanders off its usual path is, for that moment, aberrated.
senses.whyCN: 道德义从空间义长出来：心念一旦离开平常的轨道，那一刻它就是“偏了”。

senses.title: A repeatable error in measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量偏差：仪器每次都偏那么一点
senses.definition: a repeatable deviation of an instrument or a measurement from the true value
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或测量结果对真值产生的、可重复出现的偏差
senses.example: The survey was corrected for a slight aberration in the theodolite.
senses.exampleCN: 测量队对经纬仪的一处轻微偏差做了修正。
senses.why: In optics and metrology the word names an error that returns every time, not a random slip. It is the instrument's signature.
senses.whyCN: 在光学与计量学里，这个词指每次都重现的误差，而不是偶然的滑脱；它是仪器留下的签名。

senses.title: Distortion in a lens image
senses.titleCN: 光学像差：镜头把一点摊成一片
senses.definition: a defect in which a lens or mirror fails to bring light to a single sharp focus, so the image is blurred or coloured at the edges
senses.definitionCN: 透镜或反射镜不能把光汇聚到一个清晰焦点，使图像模糊或边缘带色的缺陷
senses.example: Stars near the edge of the photograph show coma, a common aberration.
senses.exampleCN: 照片边缘的恒星出现彗差，这是一种常见的像差。
senses.why: Here the deviation belongs to the optical system, not the observer: rays wander away from the ideal focus point.
senses.whyCN: 这里的偏离属于光学系统而非观测者：光线离开了理想的焦点。

senses.title: The apparent shift of starlight
senses.titleCN: 光行差：星星看起来挪了位置
senses.definition: the apparent displacement of a celestial object caused by the observer's motion combined with the finite speed of light
senses.definitionCN: 观测者运动与光速有限共同造成的天体视位置偏移
senses.example: Bradley discovered the aberration of light while searching for stellar parallax.
senses.exampleCN: 布拉德利在寻找恒星视差时发现了光行差。
senses.why: The star does not move; the observer's motion tilts the incoming ray. The same Latin word now covers a wandering of light itself.
senses.whyCN: 恒星并没有动，是观测者的运动把入射光线倾斜了。同一个拉丁词现在覆盖了光本身的“游走”。

senses.title: A deviation in a living form
senses.titleCN: 生物畸变：长歪了的结构
senses.definition: a structural or chromosomal deviation from the normal form of an organism
senses.definitionCN: 生物体在结构或染色体上偏离正常形态
senses.example: The laboratory screened the tissue for chromosomal aberrations.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室筛查了该组织的染色体畸变。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the optical term: a chromosome that departs from the standard pattern is read like a distorted image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了光学词：偏离标准模式的染色体，被读成一张走形的图像。

senses.title: A short disturbance of mind
senses.titleCN: 精神失常：短暂地离开清醒
senses.definition: a brief period of mental disturbance in which reasoning or perception departs from normal
senses.definitionCN: 一段短暂的精神紊乱，推理或感知偏离正常
senses.example: The old records describe bouts of aberration in which he spoke to people who were not there.
senses.exampleCN: 旧档案记载了他几次精神失常，对着并不存在的人说话。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century psychiatry used aberration for a mind off its track, keeping the root image of wandering.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪精神病学用 aberration 指偏离轨道的心智，保留了“游走”的词根意象。

senses.title: A point that breaks a trend
senses.titleCN: 数据里的离群点
senses.definition: an observation that departs so far from the pattern of the data that it has to be treated separately
senses.definitionCN: 偏离数据整体模式太远、需要单独处理的观测值
senses.example: The analyst set the December spike aside as an aberration.
senses.exampleCN: 分析员把十二月那个尖峰当作离群点单独搁置。
senses.why: Statistics applies the same test as astronomy: one point has left the expected curve and must be explained.
senses.whyCN: 统计学用的是和天文一样的判断：有一个点离开了预期的曲线，必须解释它为什么离开。

intro.en: Aberration is built from two Latin pieces, ab- 'away' and errare 'to wander'. It reached English through astronomy and optics before it was ever used of people.
intro.cn: aberration 由两个拉丁成分构成：ab-“离开”与 errare“游走”。它先经天文学与光学进入英语，很久以后才用来形容人。

items.en: Errare meant to wander, stray, or roam, and is also the source of English error. A wanderer is not lost yet, only off the road.
items.cn: errare 意为游走、迷路、漫游，也是英语 error 的来源。游走的人尚未“失去”，只是离开了路。

items.en: The prefix ab- marks motion away from a point. Joined to a verb of motion it produces the idea of going off in the wrong direction.
items.cn: 前缀 ab- 表示“离开某点”的运动。与移动动词结合，就产生“朝错误方向走开”的意思。

items.en: To wander away from the proper path, hence to go astray or deviate. The word is spatial before it is moral.
items.cn: 偏离正道走开，因而“走入歧途、偏离”。这个词先有空间义，后有道德义。

items.en: A wandering off, a deviation. In classical Latin it could also mean a diversion or relief, an aside that turns the mind away; that cheerful sense did not survive into English.
items.cn: 偏离、走开。古典拉丁语中它还可指“消遣、散心”，即把心思引开的插曲；这个轻松义没有进入英语。

items.en: English borrowed the word for technical deviations: the apparent motion of light and the defects of lenses and mirrors.
items.cn: 英语 16 世纪借入该词，用于技术性的偏离：光的视运动，以及透镜与反射镜的缺陷。

items.en: The sense widened in the 18c-19c to behaviour, mental states, biology, and finally statistics, while the optical senses remained technical.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，词义扩展到行为、精神状态、生物学，最后是统计学；光学的义项则一直保持技术性。

note.en: The first group is built from aberration itself; the second compares words for things that break a pattern, each with a different centre.
note.cn: 第一组由 aberration 自身派生；第二组比较同样表示“打破模式”的词，但各自的重心不同。

entries.definition: departing from the normal type. It describes the thing that has strayed, not the straying itself.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常类型的。它描述“已经走偏的东西”，而不是“走偏这件事”。

entries.definition: the quality or state of being aberrant. It is the abstract condition, not a single instance.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离常规的性质或状态；是抽象状态，而非某一次具体偏离。

entries.definition: relating to or caused by an aberration. It often modifies errors and effects.
entries.definitionCN: 与偏差有关的、由偏差引起的，常修饰误差与效应。

entries.definition: in optics, describing a lens or image that carries aberration. The word barely exists outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 光学中形容透镜或图像带有像差；几乎只出现在技术文献里。

entries.definition: a difference from an agreed standard or course. It is the neutral, measurable partner of aberration.
entries.definitionCN: 与约定标准或路线之间的差异；是 aberration 中性、可测量的伙伴。

entries.definition: something that does not fit a rule and cannot yet be explained. It stresses puzzlement rather than error.
entries.definitionCN: 不合规则且暂时无法解释的事物；强调困惑，而非错误。

entries.definition: the act of leaving an established way of doing something. It keeps the physical image of walking away.
entries.definitionCN: 离开既定做法；保留“走开”这一身体意象。

entries.definition: a person or thing that is simply strange. It carries no scientific measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅显得古怪的人或物，不带科学测量的意味。

entries.definition: a change in shape or meaning that twists the original. In optics it is one specific kind of aberration.
entries.definitionCN: 使原形或原意扭曲的变化；在光学中它只是像差的一种。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus errare 'to wander'. The same errare gives English error; the same word family gives aberrant and aberrance.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 errare“游走”。同一个 errare 也给出英语 error；同一词族还有 aberrant、aberrance。

normal.en: Ab- is away, err is wander: aberration is a wander away from the line.
normal.cn: ab- 是离开，err 是游走：aberration 就是离开那条线去游荡。

normal.en: Error and aberration are cousins: both come from Latin errare, to wander.
normal.cn: error 与 aberration 是表亲：都来自拉丁语 errare“游走”。

normal.en: In a lens, the rays wander off the focus and the star grows a halo.
normal.cn: 在镜头里，光线游离开焦点，星星就长出一圈光晕。

normal.en: A mental aberration is the mind taking a short walk off its usual road.
normal.cn: 精神失常，就是心智离开常走的路去散了一小会儿步。

normal.en: In statistics an aberration is the one dot that refuses to sit on the curve.
normal.cn: 统计里的 aberration，就是那个不肯坐在曲线上的点。

abstract.en: Every system defines a line; aberration is the price of having a line at all.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都定义了一条线；偏差，就是拥有这条线所付的代价。

abstract.en: An aberration is only visible against an expectation.
abstract.cn: 偏差，只有在期待存在时才看得见。

abstract.en: Light, minds, and data all wander in the same grammar.
abstract.cn: 光、心智与数据，用的是同一套“游走”的语法。

examples.en: The comet's position showed a tiny aberration that the old charts had missed.
examples.cn: 彗星的位置显示出旧星图漏掉的一处微小偏差。

examples.en: The coach called the team's poor first half an aberration, not a collapse.
examples.cn: 教练把球队上半场的糟糕表现称为一时失常，而不是崩盘。

examples.en: A chromatic aberration left purple fringes along the edge of the moon.
examples.cn: 色差在月亮边缘留下一圈紫色镶边。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，别惹人”——一偏离常轨，就“啊，别惹人注意”：aberration 偏离、反常

root: 源自拉丁语 aberrare（ab-“离开”+ errare“游走”），本义“游荡开去、偏离正道”，经 aberratio 进入英语；核心是“离开该走的那条线”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of aberration, all one movement: something leaves the line it should have followed. First in space, then in behaviour, instruments, light, living forms, minds, and finally data.
sensesIntro.cn: aberration 的八个义项都围绕同一个动作：某样东西离开了它本该跟随的线。先是在空间里，然后是行为、仪器、光、生物形态、心智，最后是数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight track with one short arc bending away from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条笔直的轨道，旁边岔出一小段弯出去的弧。

chain: ABERRARE = TO WANDER OFF THE PATH
A DEPARTURE FROM THE EXPECTED LINE
ANY FORM THAT LEAVES ITS PATTERN

branches.en: DEVIATION FROM A LINE: a general exception and a statistical outlier are both points off the fitted curve.
branches.cn: 偏离那条线：一般性的例外与统计离群点，都是落在拟合曲线之外的点。

branches.en: A MIND OFF ITS TRACK: a single lapse and a period of mental disturbance apply the same metaphor to judgement.
branches.cn: 离开轨道的心智：一时糊涂与一段精神紊乱，都是把同一比喻用在判断力上。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT ERROR: the deviation is built into the tool and repeats itself.
branches.cn: 仪器误差：偏差被造进工具里，并且会重复出现。

branches.en: LIGHT THAT MISSES THE FOCUS: a lens defect and the apparent shift of starlight both bend rays away from the ideal point.
branches.cn: 错过焦点的光：镜头缺陷与星光视偏移，都把光线弯离理想的那个点。

branches.en: FORM OFF ITS PATTERN: a chromosome or organ that departs from the standard shape.
branches.cn: 离开模式的形态：偏离标准形状的染色体或器官。

intro.en: Aberration carries the Latin prefix ab- and the suffix -ion. English builds the rest of the family with -ant, -ance, -al, and -ed.
intro.cn: aberration 带着拉丁前缀 ab- 与后缀 -ion；英语用 -ant、-ance、-al、-ed 造出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is errare 'to wander', ab- 'away', aberrare 'to go astray', and the noun aberratio. All four are real Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 errare“游走”、ab-“离开”、aberrare“走入歧途”，以及名词 aberratio。四个都是真实的拉丁形式。

items.meaning: departing from the normal type
items.meaningCN: 偏离正常类型的（-ant 构成形容词）
items.example: The aberrant reading was checked against a second instrument.
items.exampleCN: 那个异常读数被拿去用第二台仪器核对。

items.meaning: the state of being aberrant
items.meaningCN: 偏离常规的状态（-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: The botanist noted the aberrance of the leaf shape.
items.exampleCN: 植物学家记下了叶形的异常。

items.meaning: an instance or condition of deviation
items.meaningCN: 偏离的实例或状况（-ancy 为 -ance 的变体）
items.example: The committee reported several aberrancies in the accounts.
items.exampleCN: 委员会报告了账目中的若干异常。

items.meaning: relating to or caused by an aberration
items.meaningCN: 与偏差有关的、由偏差引起的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The signal was dismissed as an aberrational blip.
items.exampleCN: 那个信号被当作偏差性的短暂脉冲排除了。

items.meaning: carrying optical aberration
items.meaningCN: 带有光学像差的（-ate + -ed 构成技术分词）
items.example: An aberrated wavefront blurs the image.
items.exampleCN: 带像差的波前会使图像模糊。

items.meaning: the apparent shift of a star caused by the observer's motion
items.meaningCN: 观测者运动造成的恒星视位置偏移（固定术语）
items.example: The aberration of light was measured to within a second of arc.
items.exampleCN: 光行差被测量到角秒以内的精度。

items.meaning: a change in chromosome structure or number
items.meaningCN: 染色体结构或数目的改变（技术复合词）
items.example: The screening looked for chromosomal aberration in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 筛查在样本中寻找染色体畸变。

items.meaning: blurring because a spherical lens focuses rays at different points
items.meaningCN: 球面透镜把光线聚在不同焦点而造成的模糊（光学复合词）
items.example: Stopping down the lens reduced the spherical aberration.
items.exampleCN: 缩小光圈减轻了球面像差。

items.structure: in + a moment of + aberration (fixed phrase)
items.meaning: during a brief lapse of judgement
items.meaningCN: 在一时判断失常之际（固定短语）
items.example: In a moment of aberration she told him the truth.
items.exampleCN: 在一时冲动中，她把真相告诉了他。

items.meaning: designed so that no aberration occurs
items.meaningCN: 无像差的；设计上不产生偏差的（复合形容词）
items.example: The new telescope uses an aberration-free design.
items.exampleCN: 新望远镜采用了无像差设计。

latinEntries.meaning: to wander away from the right path
latinEntries.meaningCN: 离开正道走开；走入歧途

definition_zh: 容忍；忍受；（abide by）遵守；逗留；居住；持续；等待；承受（结果）
definition_en: to put up with something, to obey a rule or accept a result, and in older or literary English to stay, dwell, wait, or last
core_image: 一个人坐在原地的石阶上，不挪地方，任凭风吹雨打也不起身。
scene: She cannot abide the smell of coffee before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 abide 是「容忍、忍受」（第 1 个义项）；句意：中午以前她受不了咖啡的味道。场景：清晨办公室、刚煮开的咖啡、有人皱眉把杯子推远。

derivatives.zh: 住所；住处（源自古过去分词）
等待；逗留（abide 去掉前缀的形式）

senses.title: To put up with something
senses.titleCN: 容忍：把不快忍在原地
senses.definition: to accept or endure something unpleasant without protest, almost always in a negative sentence
senses.definitionCN: 不加抗议地接受或忍受不快之事，几乎只用于否定句
senses.example: She cannot abide the smell of coffee before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午以前她受不了咖啡的味道。
senses.why: Cannot abide is the strongest everyday survival of the word: the old sense of standing firm under a burden has turned into refusing to stand it at all.
senses.whyCN: cannot abide 是这个词最强的生活化残留：原本“在重压下站住”的意思，变成了“根本站不住、受不了”。

senses.title: To act according to a rule
senses.titleCN: 遵守：站在规则这一边
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, decision, or promise
senses.definitionCN: 按照法律、规则、决定或承诺行事
senses.example: All members must abide by the ruling of the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都必须遵守委员会的裁决。
senses.why: Abide by began in law as to stand by a decision. Standing by it came to mean accepting its authority and acting inside it.
senses.whyCN: abide by 最初在法律语里是“站在一项决定旁边”。站在它旁边，后来就成了接受它的权威并在其中行事。

senses.title: To stay in a place
senses.titleCN: 逗留：留在原地不走
senses.definition: to remain in a place instead of leaving, now mostly literary or archaic
senses.definitionCN: 留在某处而不离开，现在多用于文学或古旧语体
senses.example: Abide here until the ferry returns.
senses.exampleCN: 留在这里，等渡船回来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: Old English bidan meant to wait and stay, and staying in one spot is waiting made visible.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：古英语 bidan 意为等待、停留；留在原地，就是把“等”看得见。

senses.title: To live in a place
senses.titleCN: 居住：停得够久就成了家
senses.definition: to have one's home in a place, used in literary or religious writing
senses.definitionCN: 在某地安家居住，用于文学或宗教文本
senses.example: The monks abided in the valley for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 僧侣们在山谷中居住了三百年。
senses.why: Dwelling is staying long enough that the place becomes home. The word keeps an archaic, slightly sacred tone.
senses.whyCN: 居住，就是停留得足够久，让那个地方成为家。这个词带着古旧而略神圣的语气。

senses.title: To last through time
senses.titleCN: 持续：在时间里站住
senses.definition: to continue to exist or remain true over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期继续存在或保持真实
senses.example: The custom has abided through wars and revolutions.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗历经战争与革命而延续下来。
senses.why: From standing firm in space to standing firm in time: what lasts is what does not give way.
senses.whyCN: 从在空间里站住，到在时间里站住：能持续的东西，就是不退让的东西。

senses.title: To wait for someone or something
senses.titleCN: 等待：坐着等它到来
senses.definition: to await a person or an event, an archaic use preserved in older literature
senses.definitionCN: 等待某人或某事的到来，为古旧用法，保存在早期文学中
senses.example: They abided the king's answer through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个冬天等待着国王的答复。
senses.why: Waiting is the core of Old English bidan. To abide an answer is to sit with the waiting until it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 等待是古英语 bidan 的核心。abide an answer 就是带着这份等待坐下去，直到答复到来。

senses.title: To remain faithful
senses.titleCN: 坚守：留在信仰里不出来
senses.definition: to remain loyal to a person, faith, or promise, especially in religious language
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、信仰或承诺保持忠诚，尤见于宗教语言
senses.example: He abided in the faith of his childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚守着童年时代的信仰。
senses.why: Religious language kept the oldest meaning alive: to abide in something is to remain inside it and not move out.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言让最古老的意义活了下来：abide in 某物，就是留在它里面，不搬出去。

senses.title: To accept a result without resisting
senses.titleCN: 承受：站到结果下面
senses.definition: to accept a verdict, outcome, or consequence without fighting it
senses.definitionCN: 不抗争地接受判决、结果或后果
senses.example: The losing side agreed to abide the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 败诉一方同意接受判决。
senses.why: Here abide means to stand under the outcome rather than fight it; the legal phrase abide the event carries the same stance.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 abide 是站到结果下面，而不是与它对抗；法律短语 abide the event 也是同一姿态。

intro.en: Abide is a Germanic verb with no Latin ancestor: Old English abidan, from a- plus bidan 'to wait, stay'. Its Latin-looking neighbours are false friends.
intro.cn: abide 是日耳曼语动词，没有拉丁语祖先：古英语 abidan，由 a- 加 bidan“等待、停留”构成。它那些像拉丁语的邻居都是假朋友。

items.en: To wait, stay, dwell, and also to experience or undergo. The simplex survives in modern English as bide, as in bide one's time.
items.cn: 意为等待、停留、居住，也有“经历、承受”之义。其简单形式在现代英语中存活为 bide，如 bide one's time。

items.en: A prefix often described as intensive or perfective, giving the sense 'forth, fully, to the end'. Etymologists disagree on its exact force here, so the prefix should be treated as uncertain.
items.cn: 这个前缀通常被解释为加强或完成，表示“向前、彻底、到底”。词源学界对它在此处的具体作用有不同意见，应视为存疑。

items.en: To remain, to wait for, to endure. The prefix adds completion to the waiting: not just to wait, but to wait it out.
items.cn: 意为留下、等待、忍耐。前缀给“等待”加了完成意味：不只是等，而是等到头。

items.en: The verb widens to mean stay, endure, and tolerate. The legal phrase abide by appears in the 15c, first of standing by a decision.
items.cn: 词义扩展为停留、忍耐、容忍。法律短语 abide by 出现于 15 世纪，最初指“站在一项决定旁边”。

items.en: Cannot abide becomes the standard way to say 'detest'. The hymn Abide with Me (1855) keeps the old 'stay with' sense in public memory.
items.cn: cannot abide 成为表达“极厌恶”的标准说法。赞美诗 Abide with Me（1855）把古老的“与我同住”义留在公众记忆里。

items.en: Everyday speech prefers tolerate, obey, stay, and last. Abide survives in fixed phrases, legal prose, and deliberately archaic or religious writing.
items.cn: 日常口语更常用 tolerate、obey、stay、last。abide 存活于固定短语、法律文本，以及有意仿古或宗教性的写作中。

note.en: The first group is the real family around abide, including its own old past participle; the second gathers words that cover one of its senses each.
note.cn: 第一组是 abide 真正的词族，包括它自己的古过去分词；第二组则各取它的一个义项来比较。

entries.definition: to wait patiently for a chance. It is abide without the prefix, and survives mainly in bide one's time.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心等待时机；是去掉前缀的 abide，主要存活于 bide one's time。

entries.definition: lasting and never fading, as in an abiding interest. It describes what stays.
entries.definitionCN: 持久不衰的，如 abiding interest；描述“留下来的东西”。

entries.definition: the act of complying with a rule, or of dwelling somewhere. It is mostly legal and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 遵守规则或居住在某处；多用于法律与正式文体。

entries.definition: a home or dwelling. It was once the past participle of abide, so 'where one abode' became 'one's abode'.
entries.definitionCN: 住所、家。它原是 abide 的过去分词，因此“一个人停留之处”变成了“他的住所”。

entries.definition: to allow something unpleasant to exist without stopping it. It is the neutral verb behind cannot abide.
entries.definitionCN: 允许不快之事存在而不制止；是 cannot abide 背后那个中性的动词。

entries.definition: to bear pain or hardship over time. It stresses duration, not permission.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间承受痛苦或艰难；强调持续，而非准许。

entries.definition: to carry out the order of a person or the requirement of a rule. It is the plain word for abide by.
entries.definitionCN: 执行人的命令或规则的要求；是 abide by 的平实说法。

entries.definition: to stay in the same place or state. It covers the archaic 'stay' sense of abide.
entries.definitionCN: 留在同一地点或状态；覆盖 abide 古旧的“停留”义。

entries.definition: to live in a place, now mostly literary. It matches the 'reside' sense of abide.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地居住，现多为文学用语；对应 abide 的“居住”义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Old English a- plus bidan 'wait, stay'. The family is bide, abiding, abidance, and the old participle abode.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：古英语 a- 加 bidan“等待、停留”。词族为 bide、abiding、abidance，以及古过去分词 abode。

normal.en: Bide is to wait; abide is to wait it out, to stay put under whatever comes.
normal.cn: bide 是等；abide 是等到头，不管来什么都待在原地。

normal.en: Abide by a rule is to stand beside it and act inside its line.
normal.cn: abide by 一条规则，就是站到它旁边，在它画的线里行动。

normal.en: Cannot abide is the negative form: the burden is too heavy to stand under.
normal.cn: cannot abide 是否定式：那个担子重得站不到它下面。

normal.en: Abode is just the old past tense turned into a noun: the place where one stayed.
normal.cn: abode 就是古老过去式变成的名词：一个人曾停留的地方。

normal.en: Abide with Me is a hymn title, and it keeps the oldest sense alive in song.
normal.cn: Abide with Me 是赞美诗标题，它让最古老的意义活在歌声里。

abstract.en: To abide is to let time pass without moving.
abstract.cn: abide，就是让时间过去而自己不挪动。

abstract.en: Endurance and obedience meet in the same posture: standing under something.
abstract.cn: 忍耐与服从在同一个姿态里相遇：站到某样东西下面。

abstract.en: The oldest words for staying are also the words for putting up with.
abstract.cn: 最古老的“停留”之词，也就是“忍受”之词。

examples.en: The tenants agreed to abide by the new noise rules.
examples.cn: 租户们同意遵守新的噪音规定。

examples.en: He could not abide the way they spoke about her.
examples.cn: 他无法忍受他们谈论她的那种方式。

examples.en: A few old customs still abide in the mountain villages.
examples.cn: 一些古老习俗仍在山村里延续。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，拜的”——站在原地“啊，拜的”不动 → abide 停留、忍耐、遵守

root: 源自古英语 abidan（a- 加强/完成 + bidan“等待、停留”），属日耳曼语源，无拉丁语祖先；核心是“留在原地等下去”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abide, one posture: staying put. A person stays in a place, stays with a rule, stays loyal, stays through pain, and finally stays under a result.
sensesIntro.cn: abide 的八个义项只有一个姿态：待住不动。人待在一个地方、待在一项规则旁、待在忠诚里、待过痛苦，最后是待在一个结果下面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person seated on the same stone step, not moving whatever the weather does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在同一级石阶上，天气怎么变都不挪动。

chain: OLD ENGLISH BIDAN = TO WAIT, STAY
A- = FORTH, THROUGH TO THE END
TO REMAIN UNDER A RULE OR BURDEN
TO LAST, AND TO ACCEPT WHAT COMES

branches.en: ENDURANCE: tolerating a smell and lasting through wars are the same refusal to give way.
branches.cn: 忍耐：忍受一种气味与历经战火而延续，都是同一种“不让步”。

branches.en: COMPLIANCE: obeying a rule and accepting a verdict are both standing under an authority.
branches.cn: 服从：遵守规则与接受判决，都是站到一个权威下面。

branches.en: STAYING IN A PLACE: a brief sojourn and a lifelong dwelling differ only in length.
branches.cn: 留在某地：短暂逗留与终身居住，只差时间长短。

branches.en: WAITING: sitting with an answer that has not yet come.
branches.cn: 等待：守着一个尚未到来的答复坐下去。

branches.en: FAITHFULNESS: remaining inside a faith instead of moving out of it.
branches.cn: 忠诚：留在一种信仰里面，而不是搬出去。

intro.en: Abide has no Latin prefix. Its only historical prefix is the Old English a-, and the modern family is built with -ing, -ance, and the old participle abode.
intro.cn: abide 没有拉丁前缀。它唯一的历史前缀是古英语 a-；现代词族由 -ing、-ance 以及古过去分词 abode 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin stage here. Abide is Germanic, from Old English abidan, and any Latin word that looks similar belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语阶段。abide 属日耳曼语，来自古英语 abidan；任何看似相似的拉丁词都属于别的词族。

items.meaning: lasting, never fading
items.meaningCN: 持久的、不消退的（-ing 构成形容词）
items.example: She has an abiding interest in early maps.
items.exampleCN: 她对早期地图有持久的兴趣。

items.meaning: compliance with a rule, or a stay in a place
items.meaningCN: 对规则的遵守，或在某处的居留（-ance 构成名词）
items.example: Abidance by the safety code is checked every month.
items.exampleCN: 每月都检查对安全规程的遵守情况。

items.structure: old past participle of abide, used as a noun
items.meaning: a dwelling place
items.meaningCN: 住所、居所（由古过去分词转为名词）
items.example: They made their abode in a cottage by the river.
items.exampleCN: 他们在河边的一间小屋安了家。

items.meaning: to wait patiently
items.meaningCN: 耐心等待（去掉 a- 前缀的简单形式）
items.example: He decided to bide his time before answering.
items.exampleCN: 他决定先等待时机再答复。

items.meaning: to obey or accept a rule or decision
items.meaningCN: 遵守或接受规则、决定（by 标记所依之物）
items.example: Both sides promised to abide by the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 双方承诺遵守该条约。

items.meaning: to stay in someone's company
items.meaningCN: 与某人同在、相伴（固定短语）
items.example: The hymn pleads, abide with me.
items.exampleCN: 那首赞美诗恳求“与我同在”。

items.meaning: obeying the law
items.meaningCN: 守法的（复合形容词）
items.example: The town is full of quiet, law-abiding citizens.
items.exampleCN: 这座镇上尽是安静守法的市民。

items.meaning: to detest something
items.meaningCN: 极讨厌、无法忍受（固定习语）
items.example: She can't abide being interrupted.
items.exampleCN: 她受不了别人打断她。

items.meaning: to accept the results of one's actions
items.meaningCN: 承担行为的后果（动词带宾语的结构）
items.example: If you break the rule, you must abide the consequences.
items.exampleCN: 若违反规则，就必须承担后果。

items.meaning: a lasting attraction or concern
items.meaningCN: 持久的兴趣或关切（固定搭配）
items.example: His abiding interest was in the history of glass.
items.exampleCN: 他长久不变的兴趣是玻璃的历史。

definition_zh: 废除；废止；取消；（法律）撤销；被废除的状态
definition_en: the act of officially putting an end to a law, system, practice, or institution, and the state of having been ended
core_image: 一张写满条款的纸被划上一道横线，然后从册子上撕下来。
scene: The abolishment of the tax took effect on the first of January.
sceneCN: 这里 abolishment 是「对某项税费的正式废除」（第 3 个义项）；句意：该税种的废除于一月一日生效。场景：财政部公告、旧税表、盖章的生效日期。

collocations.phrase: the abolishment of the death penalty

derivatives.zh: 废除（源自拉丁语的同义词）
废奴主义者；主张废除者

senses.title: The official ending of a law or system
senses.titleCN: 废除：把一条法律从册子上拿掉
senses.definition: the act of ending a law or system by official decision, so that it can no longer operate
senses.definitionCN: 通过官方决定终止某项法律或制度，使其不再运作
senses.example: The abolishment of the licensing system opened the trade to small producers.
senses.exampleCN: 许可制度的废除向小生产者打开了这个行业。
senses.why: Abolishment names the completed act, not the campaign. The law is gone from the books, and the noun records that fact.
senses.whyCN: abolishment 指完成的动作，而不是运动本身。法律已从法典中消失，这个名词记录的就是这一事实。

senses.title: The ending of a long-standing practice
senses.titleCN: 废止：让一种老做法停下来
senses.definition: the act of putting an end to a custom or habit that has been followed for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 终止一种长期沿用的习俗或习惯
senses.example: The abolishment of the daily roll call changed the mood of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 每日点名制度的废止改变了学校的气氛。
senses.why: Here the object is not a statute but a habit. The word treats a custom as something that can be struck out like a rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里废除的对象不是法令，而是习惯。这个词把习俗当作一条可以划掉的规则来处理。

senses.title: The cancellation of a tax or charge
senses.titleCN: 取消：把收费那一行划掉
senses.definition: the removal of a tax, fee, or charge so that it is no longer collected
senses.definitionCN: 取消某项税、费或收费，使其不再征收
senses.example: The abolishment of the tax took effect on the first of January.
senses.exampleCN: 该税种的废除于一月一日生效。
senses.why: Money gives the word a concrete edge: a line in the revenue book is crossed out, and people stop paying.
senses.whyCN: 钱让这个词有了具体的锋刃：收入簿上的一行被划掉，人们不再缴这笔钱。

senses.title: The elimination of an institution
senses.titleCN: 废除制度：把一整套机构撤掉
senses.definition: the ending of an institution such as slavery, a monarchy, or a privileged order
senses.definitionCN: 终止奴隶制、君主制或某种特权等级这样的制度
senses.example: The abolishment of slavery was written into the new constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 废除奴隶制被写进新宪法。
senses.why: This is the word's most famous use, because an institution is exactly what abolishment is built to remove.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最著名的用法，因为“制度”正是 abolishment 天生要移除的对象。

senses.title: A legal annulment of a statute
senses.titleCN: 撤销：法庭把条文判为无效
senses.definition: the annulment of a statute or regulation by a body with legal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由有法律权限的机构宣布某法令或规章无效
senses.example: The court ordered the abolishment of the disputed regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令撤销那项有争议的规章。
senses.why: Law treats abolishment as a technical act with a date and a signature, distinct from merely ignoring a rule.
senses.whyCN: 法律把 abolishment 当作有日期、有签字的技术性行为，与单纯“不理这条规则”不同。

senses.title: The state of having been abolished
senses.titleCN: 被废：废除之后留下的空位
senses.definition: the condition of something that no longer exists as an active rule or body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物已不再作为有效规则或机构存在的状态
senses.example: After the abolishment of the office, its files sat unread for years.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构被撤销后，它的档案多年无人翻阅。
senses.why: The -ment noun can name either the act or its result, as with many English nouns of action. Here it names the resulting emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 像许多英语动作名词一样，-ment 名词既可指动作，也可指结果。这里它指结果留下的空位。

senses.title: A formal declaration that something is void
senses.titleCN: 宣告作废：当众宣布它不再算数
senses.definition: a public or formal proclamation that a rule, title, or arrangement has no further force
senses.definitionCN: 公开或正式宣告某规则、头衔或安排不再有效
senses.example: The council issued a formal abolishment of the old charter.
senses.exampleCN: 议事会正式宣告旧特许状作废。
senses.why: The noun can stand for the document or ceremony of ending, not only the ending itself; the declaration is the visible form of the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可指“终止的文件或仪式”，而不只是终止本身；宣告是这一动作看得见的形式。

senses.title: The removal of an office or post
senses.titleCN: 裁撤：把那个职位取消
senses.definition: the ending of a position or office, usually in older administrative writing
senses.definitionCN: 取消某个职位或机构编制，多见于较早的行政文本
senses.example: The abolishment of the post of town crier saved little money but ended a tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 裁撤街头公告员一职省不了多少钱，却终结了一项传统。
senses.why: An office is a small institution, and the word treats it the same way: the post is struck from the list of established positions.
senses.whyCN: 一个职位就是一个小制度，这个词照样处理：把它从在编职位的清单上划掉。

intro.en: Abolishment is an English-made noun: the verb abolish plus -ment. Its twin abolition came straight from Latin abolitio, which is why English has two near-identical words for one act.
intro.cn: abolishment 是英语自造的名词：动词 abolish 加 -ment。它的孪生词 abolition 直接来自拉丁语 abolitio，所以英语为一个动作留下了两个几乎相同的词。

items.en: To grow or be nourished, related to alere 'to feed'. Its exact contribution to abolere is debated, so the common gloss 'destroy so that it can grow no more' is a reconstruction rather than a certainty.
items.cn: 意为生长、得到滋养，与 alere“喂养”相关。它在 abolere 中究竟起什么作用仍有争论，因此常用解释“毁掉使其不能再生长”只是构拟，并非定论。

items.en: Away, off, from. Added to a verb of growth it suggests removing the conditions under which something could continue.
items.cn: 离开、去掉、脱离。加在表示生长的动词上，暗示移除某物得以继续的条件。

items.en: To efface, destroy, annul. The word is used of blotting out a name, cancelling a law, and wiping out a memory.
items.cn: 抹去、毁灭、废止。这个词可用于抹掉一个名字、取消一条法律、清除一段记忆。

items.en: A cancelling or abolishing, and also a pardon. The Latin noun is the direct source of the English doublet abolition.
items.cn: 取消、废除，也有“赦免”之义。这个拉丁名词正是英语孪生词 abolition 的直接来源。

items.en: To abolish, recorded in the 13c and carried into Middle English as abolisshen. French supplied the verb shape that English kept.
items.cn: 废除，13 世纪已有记录，并以 abolisshen 进入中古英语。法语提供了英语保留下来的动词形态。

items.en: English adds -ment to the French-derived verb and produces abolishment. Abolition enters separately from Latin, so the two nouns divide the work by register: abolition is the standard term, abolishment the formal or legal variant.
items.cn: 英语在法语来源的动词后加 -ment，造出 abolishment。abolition 另从拉丁语进入，于是两个名词按语体分工：abolition 是标准词，abolishment 是正式或法律变体。

note.en: The first group is the abolish family, where the -ment and -ion twins sit side by side; the second compares other words for ending something officially.
note.cn: 第一组是 abolish 词族，-ment 与 -ion 两个孪生词并列其中；第二组比较其他表示“正式终止”的词。

entries.definition: to end a law, system, or practice officially. The verb names the act; the noun names it or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 正式终止法律、制度或做法。动词指动作，名词指动作或其结果。

entries.definition: the ending of a system, especially slavery. It is the standard noun and carries the historical weight of the anti-slavery movement.
entries.definitionCN: 制度的终止，尤指奴隶制。它是标准名词，承载废奴运动的历史重量。

entries.definition: a person who campaigns for an institution to be abolished. The -ist marks the agent, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 主张废除某项制度的人；-ist 标记行动者，而非动作。

entries.definition: able to be abolished. It is a legal and administrative word rather than an everyday one.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被废除的；属于法律与行政用语，而非日常词。

entries.definition: the formal cancellation of a law by the body that made it. It is the precise legal partner of abolishment.
entries.definitionCN: 由立法机关对法律作出的正式取消；是 abolishment 精确的法律伙伴。

entries.definition: the taking back of a licence, right, or permission. It withdraws an authorisation rather than ending a system.
entries.definitionCN: 收回执照、权利或许可；它撤回的是授权，而不是终止一套制度。

entries.definition: a declaration that something never had valid force. It erases the act retrospectively.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告某事物从一开始就无效；它是追溯性地抹掉那个行为。

entries.definition: the complete removal of something unwanted. It is broader and less legal than abolishment.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底移除不想要的东西；比 abolishment 更宽泛，也更少法律色彩。

entries.definition: the same act under its Latin-derived name. In modern writing it is the default choice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动作的拉丁语来源名称；在现代写作中它是默认选择。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin abolere 'to wipe out', Old French abolir, English abolish, plus -ment. The Latin twin abolition came by a separate road.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 abolere“抹去”，古法语 abolir，英语 abolish，再加 -ment。拉丁语孪生词 abolition 走的是另一条路。

normal.en: -ment turns the verb into the act: abolish plus -ment is the doing of it.
normal.cn: -ment 把动词变成动作名词：abolish 加 -ment 就是“废除这件事”。

normal.en: Abolition and abolishment are twins: one from Latin abolitio, one made in English.
normal.cn: abolition 与 abolishment 是孪生：一个来自拉丁语 abolitio，一个在英语里造出。

normal.en: To abolish is to blot a line out of the book, not just to stop obeying it.
normal.cn: 废除，是把那一行从册子上抹掉，而不只是不再遵守它。

normal.en: The most famous abolishment is the ending of slavery, an institution struck from the constitution.
normal.cn: 最著名的 abolishment 是废除奴隶制：一整套制度被从宪法中划掉。

normal.en: Abolishment is rarer than abolition: when you see it, the text is usually legal or formal.
normal.cn: abolishment 比 abolition 少见：看到它时，文本通常偏法律或正式。

abstract.en: To abolish is to decide that something must stop being possible.
abstract.cn: 废除，就是决定让某件事不再可能发生。

abstract.en: Every abolishment leaves a blank line where an institution used to be.
abstract.cn: 每一次废除，都在制度曾经所在的地方留下一行空白。

abstract.en: A society is partly described by what it has chosen to abolish.
abstract.cn: 一个社会，部分地由它选择废除的东西来描述。

examples.en: The abolishment of the old tariff was welcomed by the port towns.
examples.cn: 旧关税的废除受到港口城镇的欢迎。

examples.en: Historians still argue about the economic effects of the abolishment of slavery.
examples.cn: 历史学家至今仍在争论废除奴隶制的经济影响。

examples.en: The report recommended the abolishment of the post rather than a pay cut.
examples.cn: 报告建议裁撤该职位，而不是减薪。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿伯利什门特”——阿伯把不利的条款“门”一关、划掉 → abolishment 废除

root: 英语在动词 abolish（← 古法语 abolir ← 拉丁语 abolere“抹去、废止”，ab-“离开”+ olere“生长”）后加 -ment 构成；与直接来自拉丁语 abolitio 的 abolition 是同义孪生词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abolishment, one gesture: a line is drawn through something and it stops counting. The objects range from a tax to an institution to a single post.
sensesIntro.cn: abolishment 的八个义项只有一个动作：在某样东西上划一道线，它就不再算数。对象从一项税，到一整套制度，再到一个职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause-covered page crossed out and torn from the book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满条款的纸被划掉，并从册子上撕下。

branches.en: LAW: a system ended by policy and a statute annulled by a court are both struck from the books.
branches.cn: 法律：由政策终止的制度与由法院撤销的法令，都是从册子上划掉的。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND OFFICES: slavery and a town crier's post are the same kind of listed thing, one large and one small.
branches.cn: 制度与职位：奴隶制与街头公告员的职位，是同一种“在册条目”，一大一小。

branches.en: MONEY: a tax is cancelled and the revenue line goes blank.
branches.cn: 钱：一项税被取消，收入簿上的那一行就空了。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND PROCLAMATION: a custom is ended, and the ending is announced so everyone knows it no longer counts.
branches.cn: 习俗与宣告：一种做法被终止，并且当众宣布，让所有人知道它不再算数。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what remains is not the act but the empty place it left.
branches.cn: 结果：留下的不是动作，而是动作腾出的空位。

intro.en: Abolishment is built with the noun suffix -ment on a French-derived verb. Its doublet uses -ion, and the surrounding family adds -ist and -able.
intro.cn: abolishment 由名词后缀 -ment 加在法语来源的动词上构成。它的孪生词用 -ion，周围词族再加 -ist 与 -able。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is olere 'to grow', abolere 'to wipe out', and abolitio 'a cancelling'. French abolir sits between Latin and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 olere“生长”、abolere“抹去”、abolitio“取消”。法语 abolir 位于拉丁语与英语之间。

items.meaning: to end a law or system officially
items.meaningCN: 正式终止法律或制度（-ish 为英语动词化结尾）
items.example: Parliament voted to abolish the duty.
items.exampleCN: 议会投票废除该税。

items.meaning: the act of abolishing
items.meaningCN: 废除的行为（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The abolishment of the rule came after years of debate.
items.exampleCN: 该规则的废除在多年辩论之后到来。

items.meaning: the ending of a system, especially slavery
items.meaningCN: 制度的终止，尤指奴隶制（拉丁语动作名词）
items.example: The museum documents the abolition of the slave trade.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了奴隶贸易的废除。

items.meaning: a person who works to abolish an institution
items.meaningCN: 致力于废除某制度的人（-ist 表示行动者）
items.example: The abolitionist wrote pamphlets against the trade.
items.exampleCN: 那位废奴主义者撰写小册子反对奴隶贸易。

items.meaning: possible to abolish
items.meaningCN: 可被废除的（-able 表示可能性）
items.example: The committee asked whether the levy was abolishable by decree.
items.exampleCN: 委员会询问该征税能否由法令废除。

items.meaning: still in force; not yet ended
items.meaningCN: 尚未废除的；仍然有效的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Several unabolished statutes still mention the old currency.
items.exampleCN: 若干未废除的法规仍提到旧货币。

items.meaning: the historical ending of the slave system
items.meaningCN: 奴隶制的历史性废除（固定短语）
items.example: The painting commemorates the abolishment of slavery.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画纪念奴隶制的废除。

items.meaning: an official, recorded ending
items.meaningCN: 正式且有记录的废除（固定搭配）
items.example: Only formal abolishment would satisfy the court.
items.exampleCN: 只有正式废除才能让法院满意。

items.meaning: an ending with no exceptions or remnants
items.meaningCN: 无例外、无残留的彻底废除（固定搭配）
items.example: They demanded total abolishment, not a gradual phase-out.
items.exampleCN: 他们要求彻底废除，而不是逐步淘汰。

items.meaning: to demand that something be ended
items.meaningCN: 呼吁废除某事物（动词短语结构）
items.example: Doctors called for the abolishment of the fee.
items.exampleCN: 医生们呼吁取消这项收费。

definition_zh: 突然的；意外的；唐突的；生硬的；（坡）陡峭的；不连贯的；突然中止的；（植物）截形的
definition_en: sudden and unexpected, short or rude in manner, steep, jerky, or ending without transition
core_image: 一条路走到半途忽然断掉，断面平整，下面就是陡坡。
scene: The meeting came to an abrupt end when the power failed.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 是「突然中止的」（第 5 个义项）；句意：停电让会议突然中断。场景：会议室灯灭、投影幕变黑、有人还在说话。

senses.title: Sudden and unexpected
senses.titleCN: 突然：事情没有过渡就来了
senses.definition: happening quickly and without warning, so that there is no time to prepare
senses.definitionCN: 发生得快且毫无预警，来不及准备
senses.example: An abrupt change in the wind caught the sailors off guard.
senses.exampleCN: 风向的突然变化让水手们措手不及。
senses.why: Latin abrumpere is to break off. An abrupt event is one that breaks into the expected sequence instead of flowing from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abrumpere 是“折断”。突然的事件，就是打断预期序列，而不是从序列中自然流出。

senses.title: Short and rude in manner
senses.titleCN: 唐突：话像被截断一样短
senses.definition: speaking in very few words, in a way that seems rude or unfriendly
senses.definitionCN: 说话极简短，显得无礼或不友善
senses.example: His abrupt reply made the room go quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他生硬的回答让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: A curt answer cuts the conversation short, as if the sentence were broken off. The social sense borrows the physical image of a sudden break.
senses.whyCN: 生硬的回答把对话截短，好像句子被折断。社交义借用了“突然断裂”的身体意象。

senses.title: Steep and almost vertical
senses.titleCN: 陡峭：地面忽然落下
senses.definition: rising or falling very steeply, with little slope in between
senses.definitionCN: 上升或下降极陡，中间几乎没有缓冲坡度
senses.example: The path ended at an abrupt drop of thirty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 小路尽头是一道三十米的陡落。
senses.why: A cliff that breaks off instead of sloping down is abrupt in the most literal sense: the surface simply stops and falls.
senses.whyCN: 崖壁没有缓缓下斜，而是直接断开，这就是最字面的 abrupt：表面到此为止，然后下落。

senses.title: Jerky or uneven in movement
senses.titleCN: 顿挫：动作一顿一顿地断开
senses.definition: moving in short, sharp movements rather than smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 以短促、尖锐的动作移动，而不是平滑移动
senses.example: The old truck gave an abrupt lurch and stalled.
senses.exampleCN: 旧卡车猛地一顿，然后熄火了。
senses.why: Motion that is broken into pieces is literally broken motion. Smoothness is continuity; abruptness is a series of cuts.
senses.whyCN: 被切成碎片的运动，就是字面上“断开的运动”。平滑即连续；突然即一连串切口。

senses.title: Ending without transition
senses.titleCN: 突然中止：话没说完就停
senses.definition: ending or stopping suddenly, with no preparation or closing passage
senses.definitionCN: 毫无铺垫或收束地突然结束或停止
senses.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end when the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 停电让会议突然中断。
senses.why: Here the break falls on the end of something. What is missing is the bridge that would normally carry one part into the next.
senses.whyCN: 这里的断裂落在某事物的结尾。缺少的是那座通常把前后两部分接起来的桥。

senses.title: Disconnected in speech or writing
senses.titleCN: 不连贯：句子之间没有桥
senses.definition: changing topic or direction with so little linking that the parts seem disjointed
senses.definitionCN: 转换话题或方向时缺少连接，使各部分显得脱节
senses.example: The essay's abrupt shifts made the argument hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 文章中生硬的转折让论证很难跟上。
senses.why: A discourse can be abrupt when its joints are missing. The reader feels the cut where a transition should have been.
senses.whyCN: 一段话语若缺少接缝，就会显得突兀。读者会在本该有过渡的地方感到那一道切口。

senses.title: Sudden in onset
senses.titleCN: 骤发：症状一下子就来了
senses.definition: beginning suddenly rather than developing gradually, used of symptoms and attacks
senses.definitionCN: 症状或发作一开始就很急，而非逐渐发展
senses.example: The patient reported an abrupt onset of chest pain.
senses.exampleCN: 病人主诉胸痛骤然发作。
senses.why: Medicine measures time in onset curves. An abrupt onset has no gentle rise; the line jumps.
senses.whyCN: 医学用起病曲线来量时间。骤发没有平缓的上升段，曲线是跳上去的。

senses.title: Terminating sharply in form
senses.titleCN: 截形：形状到边界就断
senses.definition: in botany and geology, ending in a sharp or flattened edge instead of tapering
senses.definitionCN: 植物学与地质学中，以锐利或平截的边缘结束，而不是逐渐变细
senses.example: The species is identified by its abrupt leaf base.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种以其截形的叶基为识别特征。
senses.why: Technical description uses the same geometry: a form that stops at a line instead of narrowing to a point.
senses.whyCN: 技术描述用的是同一套几何：形状在一条线上停住，而不是收细成一个尖。

intro.en: Abrupt is Latin abruptus, the past participle of abrumpere 'to break off'. English took the whole participle in the 16c, so the adjective is literally 'broken away'.
intro.cn: abrupt 就是拉丁语 abruptus，动词 abrumpere“折断”的过去分词。英语在 16 世纪整块借入这个分词，因此这个形容词字面上就是“被折断、断开的”。

items.en: To break, burst, or tear. It is the source of rupture, interrupt, and erupt, and it always involves a violent separation.
items.cn: 折断、爆裂、撕裂。它是 rupture、interrupt、erupt 的来源，总含暴力分离之意。

items.en: Away from. With rumpere it marks a break that separates one part from the rest.
items.cn: 离开。与 rumpere 结合，标记一种把某部分从其余部分分离出去的断裂。

items.en: To break off, to sever. The image is a branch torn from a tree rather than a crack running through it.
items.cn: 折断、切断。画面是一根枝条从树上被扯下，而不是裂纹在内部蔓延。

items.en: The past participle means broken off, steep, or disconnected. Latin already used it of cliffs and of speech.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为“被折断的、陡峭的、不连贯的”。拉丁语已用它形容崖壁和言语。

items.en: English borrows the participle whole as an adjective. The first uses are physical: a broken edge, a steep place.
items.cn: 英语把整个分词借来作形容词。最早的用法是物理性的：断开的边缘、陡峭之处。

items.en: The sense spreads from surfaces to time and to people: an abrupt stop, an abrupt manner. The metaphor is always the same cut.
items.cn: 词义从表面扩展到时间，再到人：突然的停止、生硬的态度。比喻始终是同一道切口。

note.en: The first group is the abrupt family plus a false friend that shares the root rumpere; the second separates suddenness from rudeness and from steepness.
note.cn: 第一组是 abrupt 词族，外加一个共享 rumpere 词根的假朋友；第二组把“突然”“无礼”“陡峭”分开。

entries.definition: in a sudden or curt way. It tells how something happened, not what it was.
entries.definitionCN: 以突然或生硬的方式；描述“怎样发生”，而非“是什么样”。

entries.definition: the quality of being abrupt. It names the property shared by all eight senses.
entries.definitionCN: 突然、唐突的性质；命名八个义项共有的属性。

entries.definition: a sudden breaking off or separation, used in medicine and geology.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的断裂或分离，用于医学与地质学。

entries.definition: to burst out. It shares Latin rumpere but takes e- 'out' instead of ab- 'away', so it is not a relative of abrupt in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 爆发、喷出。它共享拉丁语 rumpere，但用 e-“向外”而非 ab-“离开”，因此与 abrupt 在意义上并非同族。

entries.definition: happening without warning. It is the plain everyday partner of abrupt and carries no rudeness.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无预警地发生；是 abrupt 平实的日常伙伴，不含无礼意味。

entries.definition: extremely steep, or done with reckless haste. It joins the cliff sense and the suddenness sense.
entries.definitionCN: 极陡的，或鲁莽仓促的；同时连接“陡崖”与“突然”两个义项。

entries.tag: short to the point of rudeness
entries.definition: using so few words that the reply feels cut off. It covers the manner sense only.
entries.definitionCN: 用词少到让回答显得被截断；只覆盖“态度”义项。

entries.definition: direct in a way that seems harsh. It is abruptness of manner with an added edge of roughness.
entries.definitionCN: 直率得显得严厉；是态度上的 abrupt，再加一层粗砺。

entries.definition: rising or falling at a sharp angle. It is the terrain sense without the notion of breaking off.
entries.definitionCN: 以锐角上升或下降；只表示地形，不含“折断”的意味。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus rumpere 'to break'. The same root gives interrupt, erupt, and rupture.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 rumpere“折断”。同一词根给出 interrupt、erupt、rupture。

normal.en: Ab- away, rupt break: abrupt is something broken off from what came before.
normal.cn: ab- 离开，rupt 折断：abrupt 就是从前面断开的东西。

normal.en: An abrupt reply is a sentence with its polite ending torn off.
normal.cn: 生硬的回答，就是一句被扯掉礼貌结尾的话。

normal.en: An abrupt cliff is a slope that did not bother to slope.
normal.cn: 陡峭的崖壁，是一段懒得“斜”的坡。

normal.en: Rupture, interrupt, erupt: all of them are breaks, but only ab- means away.
normal.cn: rupture、interrupt、erupt 都是断裂，但只有 ab- 表示“离开”。

normal.en: If a curve jumps instead of rising, the onset is abrupt.
normal.cn: 曲线不是升上去而是跳上去，起病就是骤发。

abstract.en: Abruptness is what continuity looks like when it fails.
abstract.cn: 突然，就是连续性失败时的样子。

abstract.en: A break can be a cliff, a sentence, or a silence.
abstract.cn: 一道断裂，可以是崖壁、一句话，或一片沉默。

abstract.en: The same cut that frees a branch also makes it fall.
abstract.cn: 让枝条脱离的那一刀，也让它坠落。

examples.en: The road turned abruptly and then climbed the ridge.
examples.cn: 道路突然转弯，随后爬上山脊。

examples.en: His abrupt departure left the project without a leader.
examples.cn: 他的突然离开让项目失去了负责人。

examples.en: The rock face rises in an abrupt wall above the beach.
examples.cn: 岩壁在海滩上方陡然立起。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，不拉普特”——话到一半“额”一声就断掉 → abrupt 突然的、唐突的

root: 源自拉丁语 abruptus，即 abrumpere（ab-“离开”+ rumpere“折断”）的过去分词，本义“被折断、断开的”；核心是“在应当连续的地方断掉”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abrupt, one geometry: a break where a connection was expected. It can break time, speech, terrain, motion, a text, or a symptom curve.
sensesIntro.cn: abrupt 的八个义项只有一个几何形状：在本该连接的地方断掉。它可以断开时间、言语、地形、动作、文章，或一条症状曲线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path that stops at a clean edge, with a sheer drop below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在平整的断口处停住，下面就是直落。

chain: A SUDDEN CUT IN TIME OR SPEECH

branches.en: SUDDEN TIMING: an unexpected change and a sudden symptom both jump the curve instead of rising.
branches.cn: 突然的时间：意外的变化与骤发的症状，都是跳过曲线而不是沿着它上升。

branches.en: CUT SHORT: a curt reply and a meeting that stops mid-sentence are the same severed ending.
branches.cn: 被截断：生硬的回答与说到一半就停的会议，是同一个被切掉的结尾。

branches.en: STEEP TERRAIN: the ground stops sloping and simply drops.
branches.cn: 陡峭地形：地面不再斜下去，而是直接落下。

branches.en: JERKY MOTION: movement broken into sharp pieces instead of flowing.
branches.cn: 顿挫动作：运动被切成尖锐的碎片，而不是流动。

branches.en: BROKEN CONTINUITY: a text without transitions and a leaf that ends at a line share the missing taper.
branches.cn: 断裂的连续：没有过渡的文章与在一条线上终止的叶子，都缺少那段渐细。

intro.en: Abrupt is a Latin participle used as an adjective. English builds adverbs and nouns from it with -ly, -ness, and -ion.
intro.cn: abrupt 是一个作形容词用的拉丁分词。英语用 -ly、-ness、-ion 从它造出副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is rumpere 'to break', ab- 'away', abrumpere 'to break off', and abruptus 'broken off'. Abruptio is the matching noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 rumpere“折断”、ab-“离开”、abrumpere“折断离开”、abruptus“被折断的”。abruptio 是对应的名词。

items.meaning: in a sudden or curt manner
items.meaningCN: 突然地、生硬地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The music stopped abruptly.
items.exampleCN: 音乐戛然而止。

items.meaning: the quality of being abrupt
items.meaningCN: 突然、唐突的性质（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The abruptness of his tone surprised everyone.
items.exampleCN: 他语气的生硬让所有人吃惊。

items.meaning: a sudden breaking off
items.meaningCN: 突然断裂、分离（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The geologist mapped the abruption in the rock layer.
items.exampleCN: 地质学家绘制了岩层中的断裂。

items.meaning: premature separation of the placenta
items.meaningCN: 胎盘早剥（拉丁语医学术语）
items.example: Abruptio placentae requires immediate surgery.
items.exampleCN: 胎盘早剥需要立即手术。

items.meaning: a change with no warning or transition
items.meaningCN: 毫无预警或过渡的变化（固定搭配）
items.example: Climate records show an abrupt change at the end of the ice age.
items.exampleCN: 气候记录显示冰期结束时有一次突变。

items.meaning: a sudden stop
items.meaningCN: 猛然停止（固定搭配）
items.example: The train came to an abrupt halt.
items.exampleCN: 列车猛然停住。

items.meaning: a short, unfriendly way of behaving
items.meaningCN: 生硬、不友好的举止（固定搭配）
items.example: His abrupt manner hides a shy person.
items.exampleCN: 他生硬的态度掩盖着一个害羞的人。

items.meaning: a sudden beginning of symptoms
items.meaningCN: 症状的骤然发作（医学搭配）
items.example: The fever had an abrupt onset.
items.exampleCN: 发热起病很急。

items.meaning: a sharp bend with no easement
items.meaningCN: 没有缓和段的急弯（技术搭配）
items.example: Drivers slow down before the abrupt curve.
items.exampleCN: 司机在急弯前减速。

items.meaning: a leaf base that ends in a straight edge
items.meaningCN: 以平直边缘结束的叶基（植物学术语）
items.example: The key separates species by the abrupt leaf base.
items.exampleCN: 检索表以截形叶基区分物种。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被折断的；陡峭的；不连贯的

definition_zh: 突然地；意外地；唐突地；生硬地；陡然地；猛然地；不连贯地；骤发地
definition_en: in a sudden, curt, steep, jerky, or disconnected manner, with no transition before or after
core_image: 一段正在播放的录音被人直接按下停止键，声音在一个字中间被切断。
scene: She stopped speaking abruptly when she saw who had entered.
sceneCN: 这里 abruptly 是「突然地、毫无过渡地」（第 1 个义项），并与第 2 个义项“生硬”相邻；句意：一看见进来的是谁，她就突然住口。场景：半句悬在空中、门口的人影、旁人的目光。

senses.title: Suddenly and without warning
senses.titleCN: 突然：连个招呼都不打
senses.definition: in a way that happens quickly and unexpectedly, leaving no time to react
senses.definitionCN: 发生得又快又意外，来不及反应
senses.example: The storm arrived abruptly, before the boats could return.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴来得突然，船还没来得及回港。
senses.why: The adverb adds manner to the adjective: the break is not only present, it is how the event entered the scene.
senses.whyCN: 副词给形容词加了“方式”：断裂不仅存在，而且事件就是以这种方式闯入场景的。

senses.title: Curtly and unfriendlily
senses.titleCN: 生硬：把话说到一半就收回
senses.definition: in a short, sharp way that seems rude or dismissive
senses.definitionCN: 以简短、尖锐的方式，显得无礼或轻慢
senses.example: He answered abruptly and turned back to his paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他生硬地答了一句，又转回他的文件。
senses.why: Speaking abruptly is speaking with the social ending cut off. The adverb makes the cut audible in the voice.
senses.whyCN: 说话 abrupt，就是说话时把社交性的结尾切掉。副词让这道切口在声音里听得见。

senses.title: Steeply, with a sheer drop
senses.titleCN: 陡然地：地面直接落下去
senses.definition: with a very sharp slope, falling or rising almost vertically
senses.definitionCN: 坡度极陡，几乎垂直地下降或上升
senses.example: Beyond the ridge the ground drops abruptly to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊之外，地面陡然落向河边。
senses.why: The adverb describes the shape of the fall: not a gradual slope but a line that turns down.
senses.whyCN: 副词描述“落”的形状：不是缓缓倾斜，而是一条线直接折下去。

senses.title: With a sudden stop
senses.titleCN: 猛然：正在动的东西被按住
senses.definition: stopping or halting in a single sharp movement
senses.definitionCN: 以一次短促、尖锐的动作停止
senses.example: The car braked abruptly at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在路口猛然刹车。
senses.why: Here the break falls on motion. What was continuous becomes a stop with no deceleration curve.
senses.whyCN: 这里的断裂落在运动上：原本连续的动作变成一次没有减速曲线的停止。

senses.title: Without a transition in a text
senses.titleCN: 不连贯地：段落之间没有桥
senses.definition: in a way that jumps from one point to another without linking words or steps
senses.definitionCN: 从一个论点跳到另一个，缺少连接词或过渡步骤
senses.example: The chapter ends abruptly, leaving the reader mid-scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章结束得很突兀，把读者留在场景中间。
senses.why: A text can be cut as surely as a road. The adverb marks the missing bridge between two parts.
senses.whyCN: 文本可以像道路一样被切断。副词标记的是两部分之间那座缺失的桥。

senses.title: With a sudden break in sound
senses.titleCN: 戛然：声音被一刀切掉
senses.definition: of music or noise, stopping in the middle rather than fading or resolving
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或声响在中间停住，而不是渐弱或收束
senses.example: The recording cuts off abruptly in the second verse.
senses.exampleCN: 录音在第二段歌词中戛然而止。
senses.why: Sound is the clearest place to hear abruptness: a wave that should decay is instead sliced.
senses.whyCN: 声音是听见 abrupt 最清楚的地方：本该衰减的声波，被直接切断了。

senses.title: With a sudden onset
senses.titleCN: 骤发地：症状一下子就出现
senses.definition: beginning suddenly rather than building up, used of illnesses and attacks
senses.definitionCN: 一开始就很急，而非逐渐累积，用于疾病与发作
senses.example: The headache began abruptly during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 头痛在讲座进行中骤然开始。
senses.why: Medical writing uses the adverb to place the start of a symptom precisely: the onset line jumps.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作里，这个副词用来精确放置症状的起点：起病线是跳上去的。

senses.title: In a cut-off or truncated way
senses.titleCN: 被截断地：话没说完就没了
senses.definition: ending before the expected completion, as if the remaining part were removed
senses.definitionCN: 在预期完成之前就结束，好像剩下的部分被移除
senses.example: The announcement was cut off abruptly by static.
senses.exampleCN: 公告被静电噪声突然截断。
senses.why: Truncation is the purest form of the image: a line that stops, with the rest simply absent.
senses.whyCN: 截断是这幅意象最纯粹的形式：一条线停住，其余部分干脆不存在。

intro.en: Abruptly is abrupt plus the Germanic adverb suffix -ly. The Latin part ends at abruptus; the -ly ending has its own Old English history and is not Latin at all.
intro.cn: abruptly 是 abrupt 加日耳曼语副词后缀 -ly。拉丁语部分到 abruptus 为止；-ly 有自己的古英语历史，根本不是拉丁语。

items.en: The adverb suffix came from lic, meaning body, form, or manner. -lice meant 'in the manner of', and it is the ancestor of modern -ly.
items.cn: 这个副词后缀来自 lic，意为身体、形状、方式。-lice 表示“以……的方式”，是现代 -ly 的祖先。

items.en: The same word became the adjective suffix -ly and the noun lich, a body. English -ly is Germanic, not Latin.
items.cn: 同一个词还变成形容词后缀 -ly 与名词 lich（身体）。英语的 -ly 属日耳曼语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: The suffix shortened to -li and merged with the adjective suffix, so that a word like kindly could be either adjective or adverb.
items.cn: 后缀缩短为 -li，并与形容词后缀合并，因此 kindly 这类词当时既可作形容词也可作副词。

items.en: The base word entered English in the 16c as abrupt, a past participle meaning broken off. It supplies the meaning, not the ending.
items.cn: 词基在 16 世纪以 abrupt 进入英语，是一个意为“被折断”的过去分词。它提供意义，不提供词尾。

items.en: Abrupt + -ly produces abruptly. Early uses describe physical breaks and steep ground; the manner sense follows soon after.
items.cn: abrupt 加 -ly 造出 abruptly。早期用法描述物理断裂与陡地，态度义随后出现。

items.en: The adverb becomes the standard way to modify verbs of stopping, ending, changing, and speaking, while the adjective keeps the descriptive load.
items.cn: 这个副词成为修饰 stop、end、change、speak 等动词的标准方式；形容词则继续承担描述性的分量。

note.en: The first group is the abrupt family plus one look-alike that shares rumpere but not ab-; the second separates the kinds of manner the adverb can express.
note.cn: 第一组是 abrupt 词族，外加一个共享 rumpere 却不共享 ab- 的形近词；第二组区分这个副词能表达的各种方式。

entries.definition: sudden, curt, steep, or cut short. It describes the thing; abruptly describes the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的、生硬的、陡的或被截断的；描述事物本身，而 abruptly 描述做事的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being abrupt. It turns the adverb's manner back into a property.
entries.definitionCN: 突然、唐突的性质；把副词的方式再变回属性。

entries.definition: a sudden separation or breaking off, as of rock layers or the placenta.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的分离或断裂，如岩层或胎盘。

entries.definition: in a dishonest way. Corrupt shares Latin rumpere but takes com- 'together, completely', so it means thoroughly broken, not broken away.
entries.definitionCN: 以不诚实的方式。corrupt 共享拉丁语 rumpere，但用 com-“共同、彻底”，意为“彻底坏掉”，而非“断开离开”。

entries.definition: without warning. It is the neutral adverb of timing and says nothing about manner.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无预警地；是时间上的中性副词，不涉及态度。

entries.definition: in a blunt, slightly harsh way. It adds roughness to the curt sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以直率而略粗砺的方式；在“生硬”之上再加一层粗砺。

entries.definition: with so few words that the reply feels cut off. It is the pure manner reading of abruptly.
entries.definitionCN: 用词少到让回答像被截断；是 abruptly 纯粹的“态度”读法。

entries.definition: in a way that has a cutting edge, of tone or movement. It stresses the sting rather than the break.
entries.definitionCN: 语气或动作带锋刃；强调刺痛，而非断裂。

entries.definition: very steeply, or with reckless haste. It covers both the cliff and the timing senses.
entries.definitionCN: 极陡地，或鲁莽仓促地；同时覆盖崖壁与时间两个义项。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin abruptus 'broken off' plus Germanic -ly 'in the manner of'. The suffix is Old English, not Latin.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 abruptus“被折断的”加日耳曼语 -ly“以……方式”。这个后缀是古英语，不是拉丁语。

normal.en: Abrupt is the broken thing; abruptly is the way it breaks into the scene.
normal.cn: abrupt 是被折断的东西；abruptly 是它闯进场景的方式。

normal.en: -ly comes from Old English lic, 'body or manner', the same source as the adjective suffix.
normal.cn: -ly 来自古英语 lic“身体、方式”，与形容词后缀同源。

normal.en: A recording that stops abruptly leaves the last word hanging in the air.
normal.cn: 突然停下的录音，把最后一个词悬在空中。

normal.en: Speak abruptly and the listener hears the missing polite ending.
normal.cn: 说话 abrupt，听者听见的是那句缺失的客套结尾。

normal.en: Ground that drops abruptly is a slope that refused to slope.
normal.cn: 陡然下落的地面，是一段拒绝变斜的坡。

abstract.en: Abruptly is the adverb of unannounced endings.
abstract.cn: abruptly，是“不打招呼的结束”的副词。

abstract.en: What stops abruptly leaves a shape in the silence.
abstract.cn: 骤然停止的东西，会在寂静里留下一个形状。

abstract.en: Timing, tone, and terrain can all be cut by the same word.
abstract.cn: 时间、语气与地形，都能被同一个词切断。

examples.en: The conversation ended abruptly when the fire alarm sounded.
examples.cn: 火警响起时，谈话戛然而止。

examples.en: The land rises abruptly behind the village.
examples.cn: 村庄后面的地势陡然升高。

examples.en: He answered abruptly, then apologized for his tone.
examples.cn: 他生硬地回答，随后又为语气道歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，不拉普特利”——话说到一半“额”一声就断 → abruptly 突然地、生硬地

root: 由 abrupt（← 拉丁语 abruptus，abrumpere“折断”的过去分词，ab-“离开”+ rumpere“折断”）加日耳曼语副词后缀 -ly 构成；核心是“以断裂的方式”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abruptly, one manner: something is cut rather than continued. The cut can fall on time, tone, slope, motion, text, sound, a symptom, or a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: abruptly 的八个义项只有一种方式：某事物不是延续，而是被切断。切口可以落在时间、语气、坡度、动作、文章、声音、症状或一句话上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recording stopped mid-word, the last syllable left hanging.
core.cn: 核心意象：录音在一个词中间被按停，最后一个音节悬着。

chain: OLD ENGLISH -LICE = IN THE MANNER OF

branches.en: SUDDEN TIMING: a storm and a symptom both enter without a run-up.
branches.cn: 突然的时间：风暴与症状都是没有预热就登场。

branches.en: CURT MANNER: the sentence loses its social ending and the voice sounds cut.
branches.cn: 生硬态度：句子丢掉社交性的结尾，声音听起来是被切过的。

branches.en: STEEP GROUND: the fall is a line turned down, not a curve.
branches.cn: 陡峭地面：下落是一条折下去的线，而不是曲线。

branches.en: CUTTING OFF: a brake and a truncated announcement both stop the expected continuation.
branches.cn: 截断：刹车与被截断的公告，都终止了预期的延续。

branches.en: NO TRANSITION: a text jumping between points and music sliced mid-phrase share the missing bridge.
branches.cn: 没有过渡：在论点间跳跃的文章与在乐句中切断的音乐，都缺那座桥。

intro.en: Abruptly is one of the clearest cases of a Latin stem with a Germanic suffix: abruptus supplies the meaning, -ly supplies the adverbial grammar.
intro.cn: abruptly 是“拉丁词干 + 日耳曼后缀”最清楚的例子之一：abruptus 提供意义，-ly 提供副词语法。

latinIntro.en: Latin stops at abruptus. There is no Latin -ly; the adverb ending belongs to Old English -lice. The Latin entries below are the base forms behind abrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语到 abruptus 为止。拉丁语没有 -ly；副词词尾属于古英语 -lice。下面的拉丁条目是 abrupt 背后的词基形式。

items.meaning: in a sudden or curt manner
items.meaningCN: 以突然或生硬的方式（形容词加 -ly 构成副词）
items.example: She left abruptly without saying goodbye.
items.exampleCN: 她没告别就突然离开了。

items.meaning: broken off; sudden; curt
items.meaningCN: 被折断的；突然的；生硬的（拉丁分词作形容词）
items.example: The abrupt turn surprised the driver.
items.exampleCN: 那个急转弯让司机吃惊。

items.meaning: the state of being abrupt
items.meaningCN: 突然或唐突的状态（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The abruptness of the ending felt deliberate.
items.exampleCN: 那个结尾的突兀感像是故意的。

items.meaning: a sudden separation
items.meaningCN: 突然的断裂或分离（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The abruption left a clean face of rock.
items.exampleCN: 那次断裂留下一面平整的岩壁。

items.meaning: to cease in a single sharp movement
items.meaningCN: 以一次短促动作停止（动词搭配）
items.example: The engine stopped abruptly.
items.exampleCN: 发动机骤然停转。

items.meaning: to finish with no closing passage
items.meaningCN: 没有收束段落就结束（动词搭配）
items.example: The letter ends abruptly in mid-sentence.
items.exampleCN: 这封信在半句处突然结束。

items.meaning: to talk in a short, unfriendly way
items.meaningCN: 以简短、不友好的方式说话（动词搭配）
items.example: He spoke abruptly to the reporters.
items.exampleCN: 他对记者说话很生硬。

items.meaning: to go up with a very steep slope
items.meaningCN: 以极陡的坡度升高（动词搭配）
items.example: The cliffs rise abruptly from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 悬崖从海面陡然升起。

items.meaning: to stop in the middle of speaking
items.meaningCN: 说到一半突然停住（短语动词搭配）
items.example: She broke off abruptly and looked away.
items.exampleCN: 她突然住口，把目光移开。

items.meaning: ended as if severed
items.meaningCN: 像被切断一样终止（副词加过去分词）
items.example: The call was abruptly cut off.
items.exampleCN: 通话被突然切断。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被折断的；陡的；不连贯的

definition_zh: 吸收；吸附；（营养的）摄取；专注；并入；吸收（光、热、声）；吸附作用
definition_en: the taking in of a liquid, gas, nutrient, energy, or knowledge, and the state of being completely engaged or merged into something larger
core_image: 一块干海绵贴到水面上，水沿着孔隙往上走，表面很快变暗变重。
scene: The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
sceneCN: 这里 absorption 是「材料对水的吸收」（第 1 个义项）；句意：黏土对水的吸收延误了播种。场景：雨后的田、脚陷进去的泥、拖拉机留下的深辙。

senses.title: The uptake of liquid by a material
senses.titleCN: 吸液：孔洞把水拉进去
senses.definition: the process by which a solid takes a liquid into itself, filling its pores or spaces
senses.definitionCN: 固体把液体纳入自身、填满孔隙或空隙的过程
senses.example: The absorption of water by the clay soil delayed the planting.
senses.exampleCN: 黏土对水的吸收延误了播种。
senses.why: Latin absorbere is to suck in. The image is not a surface coating but a material pulling something inside itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absorbere 是“吸进去”。画面不是表面涂层，而是材料把某物拉进自身内部。

senses.title: The body's uptake of nutrients
senses.titleCN: 吸收营养：穿过肠壁进了身体
senses.definition: the passage of digested nutrients into the blood or body tissues
senses.definitionCN: 消化后的营养进入血液或身体组织的过程
senses.example: Poor absorption of iron can cause fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 铁吸收不良会导致疲劳。
senses.why: The body is the container here. Nutrients are not merely eaten but taken through a wall into the interior.
senses.whyCN: 这里的容器是身体。营养不只是被吃下，而是穿过一道壁进入内部。

senses.title: The taking in of knowledge
senses.titleCN: 知识的吸收：读进去、化成自己的
senses.definition: the process of understanding and remembering information so that it becomes part of one's knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 理解并记住信息，使其成为自身知识一部分的过程
senses.example: The course depends on steady absorption of new vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课依赖对新词汇的稳定吸收。
senses.why: Learning is treated as a material process: what is read is absorbed into the mind as water is absorbed into a cloth.
senses.whyCN: 学习被当作材料过程：读到的东西被吸进心里，就像水被吸进布中。

senses.title: Complete engrossment in an activity
senses.titleCN: 专注：整个人被吸进一件事
senses.definition: the state of having all one's attention taken by something, so that time and surroundings drop away
senses.definitionCN: 全部注意力被某事物占据，时间与周围环境都退去的状态
senses.example: His absorption in the problem made him miss the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个问题的专注让他错过了末班车。
senses.why: The same verb that takes liquid into a sponge takes a person into a task. The mind has no attention left on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 把水吸进海绵的那个动词，也把人吸进一项任务。心智在表面上再没留下注意力。

senses.title: The merging of an organisation
senses.titleCN: 并入：小公司被大公司吞进去
senses.definition: the incorporation of one company, group, or territory into a larger one, losing separate identity
senses.definitionCN: 一个公司、团体或地区被并入更大者，失去独立身份
senses.example: The absorption of the smaller firm took two years to complete.
senses.exampleCN: 对那家较小公司的并入花了两年才完成。
senses.why: Corporate absorption keeps the physical picture: the smaller body is taken inside the larger and no longer has an outer surface of its own.
senses.whyCN: 公司“并入”保留了物理画面：较小的实体被纳入更大者内部，不再有自己的外表面。

senses.title: The uptake of light or energy
senses.titleCN: 吸光：光子被材料收走
senses.definition: the process in which matter takes up electromagnetic radiation or energy, often converting it into heat
senses.definitionCN: 物质摄取电磁辐射或能量、常将其转为热的过程
senses.example: The dark surface showed strong absorption across the visible spectrum.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面在整个可见光谱上表现出强吸收。
senses.why: Physics names with the old verb: a photon is not reflected or transmitted but swallowed by the material.
senses.whyCN: 物理学沿用这个古老动词：光子不被反射或透射，而是被材料吞掉。

senses.title: The dissolving of a gas in a liquid
senses.titleCN: 溶解吸收：气体进了液体里面
senses.definition: the process by which gas molecules enter the bulk of a liquid rather than staying on its surface
senses.definitionCN: 气体分子进入液体内部、而非停留在表面的过程
senses.example: The absorption of carbon dioxide by seawater lowers the ocean's pH.
senses.exampleCN: 海水对二氧化碳的吸收降低了海洋的 pH。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes absorption from adsorption: here the gas goes inside the liquid, not onto a surface.
senses.whyCN: 化学区分 absorption 与 adsorption：这里气体进入液体内部，而不是附着在表面。

senses.title: The damping of sound
senses.titleCN: 吸声：声音被材料吃掉
senses.definition: the reduction of sound energy as it passes into a material, so that less is reflected back
senses.definitionCN: 声音进入材料时能量被削减、反射回来的部分减少
senses.example: The studio's walls were chosen for their low-frequency absorption.
senses.exampleCN: 录音室的墙是按低频吸声性能挑选的。
senses.why: Sound is a wave, and a porous wall takes part of it in. The energy does not vanish; it becomes a little heat inside the material.
senses.whyCN: 声音是波，多孔的墙把其中一部分收进去。能量并未消失，而是在材料内部变成一点热。

intro.en: Absorption is Latin absorptio, from absorbere 'to suck in': ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. English borrowed the noun in the 16c and later gave it technical work in physics and chemistry.
intro.cn: absorption 是拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere“吸进去”：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。英语 16 世纪借入这个名词，后来才在物理与化学中给它技术任务。

items.en: To suck in, swallow, or drink up. It describes a mouth or a porous body drawing something inward.
items.cn: 吸入、吞下、喝干。它描述嘴或多孔的身体把某物向内拉。

items.en: Away from, off. With sorbere it marks the movement of something out of its surroundings and into the absorbing body.
items.cn: 离开、脱离。与 sorbere 结合，标记某物从周围环境进入吸收者内部。

items.en: To swallow up, to take in completely. It is used of the sea swallowing a ship as well as of a sponge taking water.
items.cn: 吞没、完全纳入。它既用于大海吞没船只，也用于海绵吸水。

items.en: A swallowing up. The noun is rare in classical Latin but exactly matches the English technical need.
items.cn: 吞没、吸尽。这个名词在古典拉丁语中不常见，却正好对应英语的技术需要。

items.en: The noun enters English through learned writing. Early uses are medical and alchemical before they become physical.
items.cn: 这个名词经学术写作进入英语。早期用法属医学与炼金术，之后才转为物理学用法。

items.en: Physics, chemistry, acoustics, and business each take a share: light, gas, sound, nutrients, and companies are all absorbed. The mental sense, absorbed in a book, keeps the oldest metaphor alive.
items.cn: 物理学、化学、声学与商业各取一份：光、气体、声音、营养、公司都能被“吸收”。心智义“沉浸在一本书里”让最古老的比喻继续活着。

note.en: The first group is the absorb family plus adsorption, a look-alike with a different prefix and a genuinely different process; the second compares other kinds of taking in.
note.cn: 第一组是 absorb 词族，外加 adsorption——一个前缀不同、过程也确实不同的形近词；第二组比较其他“纳入”方式。

entries.definition: to take in liquid, energy, or information. The verb is the act; absorption is the process or state.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息；动词指动作，absorption 指过程或状态。

entries.definition: able to absorb, or a material that does so. It describes capacity, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 能吸收的，或指吸收材料；描述能力，而非事件。

entries.definition: relating to absorption. It often appears in technical phrases such as absorptive capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 与吸收有关的，常见于 absorptive capacity 等技术短语。

entries.definition: the sticking of molecules onto a surface. It uses ad- 'to' rather than ab- 'away', and is a surface process, not an uptake into the bulk.
entries.definitionCN: 分子附着在表面。它用 ad-“向”而非 ab-“离开”，是表面过程，不是吸入内部。

entries.definition: the taking in of a substance by a cell, tissue, or system. It is the neutral scientific partner.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞、组织或系统对物质的摄取；是中性的科学伙伴。

entries.definition: the process of absorbing information or a group so that it becomes part of the whole. It stresses integration after uptake.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息或群体吸收进来、使之成为整体一部分；强调摄入之后的整合。

entries.definition: the formal merging of one body into another. It is the legal form of the corporate sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一个实体正式并入另一个；是公司义的法律形式。

entries.definition: the state of having one's attention completely occupied. It is the mental sense without the physical image.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力被完全占据的状态；是去掉物理意象的心智义。

entries.definition: the reduction in strength of a signal or wave. It names the result of acoustic absorption, not the taking in.
entries.definitionCN: 信号或波强度的减弱；命名吸声的结果，而非“吸进去”的动作。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ab- 'away' plus sorbere 'to suck'. The same root gives absorb, absorbent, and absorptive; adsorption is a different prefix and a different process.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ab-“离开”加 sorbere“吸”。同一词根给出 absorb、absorbent、absorptive；adsorption 前缀不同，过程也不同。

normal.en: Ab- away, sorb suck: absorption is something sucked away into another body.
normal.cn: ab- 离开，sorb 吸：absorption 就是某物被吸走、进入另一个物体。

normal.en: A sponge does not coat itself with water; it pulls the water inside.
normal.cn: 海绵不是给自己涂上一层水，而是把水拉进内部。

normal.en: Adsorption sticks to the surface; absorption goes into the bulk. One letter, two processes.
normal.cn: adsorption 贴在表面，absorption 进入内部。差一个字母，是两种过程。

normal.en: Absorbed in a book: the reader has been taken inside the text.
normal.cn: absorbed in a book：读者被吸进文本里面。

normal.en: A dark wall absorbs light and turns it into a little heat.
normal.cn: 深色的墙吸收光，并把它变成一点热。

abstract.en: Absorption is what happens when a boundary lets something through instead of bouncing it back.
abstract.cn: 吸收，就是边界让某物通过、而不是把它弹回去。

abstract.en: To be absorbed is to have no surface left for the world.
abstract.cn: 被吸进去，就是再没有留给世界的表面。

abstract.en: Matter, mind, and companies all have pores.
abstract.cn: 物质、心智与公司，都有孔隙。

examples.en: The root hairs increase the absorption of water from the soil.
examples.cn: 根毛增加了对土壤中水的吸收。

examples.en: His absorption in the chess game made the room seem to disappear.
examples.cn: 他对棋局的专注让整个房间仿佛消失了。

examples.en: The fabric's sound absorption was measured in a test chamber.
examples.cn: 这种织物的吸声性能在测试舱中被测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额不吸哦普申”——海绵“额”一下把水吸进去 → absorption 吸收

root: 源自拉丁语 absorptio，来自 absorbere（ab-“离开”+ sorbere“吸、吞”），本义“吸进去、吞没”；核心是“把外部之物纳入内部”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of absorption, one movement: something outside passes a boundary and becomes part of what is inside. The boundary can be a pore, a gut wall, a mind, a company, or a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: absorption 的八个义项只有一个动作：外部之物越过一道边界，成为内部的一部分。边界可以是孔隙、肠壁、心智、公司，或一个表面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge touching water and pulling it up into its pores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块干海绵触到水面，把水往上拉进孔里。

branches.en: MATERIAL UPTAKE: a sponge and a seawater sample both pull a substance inside, one through pores and one through a liquid surface.
branches.cn: 材料摄入：海绵与海水样本都把物质拉进内部，一个经孔隙，一个经液面。

branches.en: THE BODY: nutrients cross a wall and become part of the organism.
branches.cn: 身体：营养穿过一道壁，成为生物体的一部分。

branches.en: THE MIND: knowledge is taken in, and a task can take the whole person in.
branches.cn: 心智：知识被吸进去，一项任务也能把整个人吸进去。

branches.en: THE ORGANISATION: a smaller firm loses its outer surface inside a larger one.
branches.cn: 组织：较小的公司在更大者内部失去自己的外表面。

branches.en: ENERGY AND SOUND: light and sound are swallowed and turned into heat rather than sent back.
branches.cn: 能量与声音：光与声被吞下、转为热，而不是被送回。

intro.en: Absorption carries Latin ab- and -tion. English builds the verb absorb, the capacity adjective absorbent, and the relational adjective absorptive.
intro.cn: absorption 带着拉丁前缀 ab- 与后缀 -tion。英语造出动词 absorb、能力形容词 absorbent，以及关系形容词 absorptive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is sorbere 'to suck', absorbere 'to suck in', and absorptio 'a swallowing up'. Adsorption is not in this chain: it uses ad- and means surface attachment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 sorbere“吸”、absorbere“吸进去”、absorptio“吞没”。adsorption 不在这个链条里：它用 ad-，意为表面附着。

items.meaning: to take in liquid, energy, or information
items.meaningCN: 吸收液体、能量或信息（拉丁动词英语化）
items.example: The paper towel absorbed the spill.
items.exampleCN: 纸巾吸干了洒出来的液体。

items.meaning: able to absorb; a material that absorbs
items.meaningCN: 能吸收的；吸收材料（-ent 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: The dressing is highly absorbent.
items.exampleCN: 这种敷料吸水性强。

items.meaning: relating to absorption
items.meaningCN: 与吸收有关的（-ive 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The absorptive capacity of the soil is low.
items.exampleCN: 这种土壤的吸收能力很低。

items.meaning: the process or state of being absorbed
items.meaningCN: 吸收的过程或被吸收的状态（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Absorption of the drug is fastest on an empty stomach.
items.exampleCN: 空腹时药物吸收最快。

items.meaning: preoccupation with oneself
items.meaningCN: 自我专注；只顾自己（复合名词）
items.example: His self-absorption made teamwork difficult.
items.exampleCN: 他的自我专注让团队合作变得困难。

items.meaning: the pattern of wavelengths a substance takes in
items.meaningCN: 物质所吸收波长的图谱（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption spectrum identified the gas.
items.exampleCN: 吸收光谱确定了这种气体。

items.meaning: the speed at which a substance is taken in
items.meaningCN: 物质被吸收的速度（技术复合词）
items.example: The absorption rate depends on temperature.
items.exampleCN: 吸收率取决于温度。

items.meaning: the uptake of water by a material or body
items.meaningCN: 材料或身体对水的吸收（固定短语）
items.example: The absorption of water by the seeds begins within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 种子对水的吸收在几分钟内就开始。

items.meaning: the damping of sound energy by a material
items.meaningCN: 材料对声能的削减（复合词）
items.example: The ceiling panels improve sound absorption.
items.exampleCN: 天花板板材改善了吸声效果。

items.meaning: the merging of a firm into another
items.meaningCN: 一家公司被并入另一家（商业短语）
items.example: The absorption of the company removed its brand from the market.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的并入使其品牌从市场上消失。

definition_zh: 大量；充裕；丰富；富足；丰盛；（生态）个体数量；（同位素）丰度；（文风）富丽；（情感的）充沛；（经济）过剩
definition_en: a very large quantity of something, wealth, or the state of having more than enough
core_image: 一只碗里的水不断上涨，越过碗沿，顺着外壁漫下来。
scene: Wild strawberries grow in abundance along the forest path.
sceneCN: 这里 abundance 是「大量、充裕」（第 1 个义项）；句意：林间小路上野草莓多得是。场景：清晨的针叶林，路边一片红点，采不完。

senses.title: A plentiful supply
senses.titleCN: 充裕：东西多到用不完
senses.definition: a quantity of something that is more than enough for what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 某物的数量超过实际所需，用之不尽
senses.example: Wild strawberries grow in abundance along the forest path.
senses.exampleCN: 林间小路上的野草莓长得极多。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to overflow. Abundance is first a quantity that spills past the edge of need, not merely a large number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是“溢出”。abundance 首先指越过“需要”这条碗沿的量，而不只是数字大。

senses.title: Wealth and prosperity
senses.titleCN: 富足：资源多到不必算计
senses.definition: a state of having a great deal of money or material goods
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱或物质资料的状态
senses.example: The town's abundance was visible in its new library and hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的富足从新图书馆和医院就能看出来。
senses.why: When overflow becomes a lasting condition rather than a single harvest, it is read as wealth. The image shifts from a filled bowl to a well-stocked household.
senses.whyCN: 当“溢出”成为长期状态而不是一次收成，它就被读作财富。意象从装满的碗，变成仓廪充实的家。

senses.title: Ecological species abundance
senses.titleCN: 物种丰度：一片地里有多少个体
senses.definition: in ecology, the number of individuals of a species in a given area or community
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中，某一地区或群落内某物种的个体数目
senses.example: The survey recorded high species abundance in the restored wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到修复后的湿地物种丰度很高。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals the way a farmer counts grain. Abundance here is a measurable total, with no implication of surplus.
senses.whyCN: 生态学数个体，就像农夫数谷粒。这里的 abundance 是可测的总量，不含“过剩”之意。

senses.title: Elemental or isotopic abundance
senses.titleCN: 丰度：某种原子在自然界占多少
senses.definition: in chemistry and astronomy, the proportion of an element or isotope found in a sample or in nature
senses.definitionCN: 化学与天文学中，某元素或同位素在样品或自然界中所占的比例
senses.example: Carbon-12 accounts for about 99 per cent of natural carbon abundance.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-12 约占天然碳丰度的百分之九十九。
senses.why: The technical sense narrows overflow into a ratio: how much of one kind is present compared with the rest. The bowl now has labelled compartments.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把“溢出”收窄成一个比值：某一种占其余部分的多少。碗里现在有了分格和标签。

senses.title: Richness of detail or style
senses.titleCN: 富丽：文字或画面上的丰盛
senses.definition: a large amount of detail, ornament, or expressive resource in a work or style
senses.definitionCN: 作品或风格中细节、装饰或表现手段的大量存在
senses.example: The novel's abundance of detail slows the reader down in a good way.
senses.exampleCN: 小说细节的丰盛以一种好的方式让读者慢下来。
senses.why: A text can overflow too. Here the surplus is not food but detail, and the metaphor moves from the bowl to the page.
senses.whyCN: 文本也会溢出。这里的过剩不是食物而是细节，比喻从碗移到了纸面。

senses.title: Great amount of feeling
senses.titleCN: 充沛：情感满到溢出来
senses.definition: an overwhelming amount of a feeling or quality, such as joy or generosity
