senses.definitionCN: 喜悦、慷慨等情感或品质强烈到难以容纳的程度
senses.example: She thanked them with an abundance of warmth.
senses.exampleCN: 她以满腔温情感谢他们。
senses.why: Feelings are described as quantities because they seem to fill a person. An abundance of warmth is warmth that exceeds the container.
senses.whyCN: 情感被当作量来描写，因为它们像能装满一个人。an abundance of warmth 就是超出容器的暖意。

senses.title: Surplus or excess
senses.titleCN: 过剩：多出来的那一部分
senses.definition: an amount so large that it becomes more than can be used, and sometimes a burden
senses.definitionCN: 数量大到超过可用限度，有时反成负担
senses.example: An abundance of caution can paralyse a committee.
senses.exampleCN: 过度的谨慎会让委员会动弹不得。
senses.why: The same overflow that delights can drown. When the emphasis falls on what spills over the edge, abundance becomes excess.
senses.whyCN: 令人欣喜的溢出也可能把人淹掉。当重心落在越过碗沿的那部分时，abundance 就成了过剩。

senses.title: Plenty as an economic condition
senses.titleCN: 丰裕：与稀缺相对的那种状态
senses.definition: in economics, a condition in which supply outstrips demand or resources are ample
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中供给超过需求、或资源充足的状态
senses.example: The debate turns on whether abundance can coexist with scarcity pricing.
senses.exampleCN: 争论的焦点在于丰裕能否与稀缺定价共存。
senses.why: Economics sets abundance against scarcity as two poles. Abundance is the pole where the bowl does not need rationing.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把丰裕与稀缺设为两极。丰裕就是那只不需要配给的碗。

intro.en: Abundance comes through Old French abondance from Latin abundantia, a noun built on abundare 'to overflow'. The root is unda, a wave, so plenty is pictured as water rising over its bank.
intro.cn: abundance 经古法语 abondance 来自拉丁语 abundantia，这个词由 abundare“溢出”构成。词根是 unda“波浪”，所以“充裕”被画成水流涨过河岸。

items.en: A wave, a moving mass of water. It survives in undulate and inundate, and it gives the whole family its liquid image.
items.cn: 波浪，一股流动的水。它留在 undulate、inundate 里，并给整个词族带来水的意象。

items.en: To flow, surge, or rise in waves. The verb already suggests water that will not stay inside its channel.
items.cn: 流动、涌动、如浪上升。这个动词已经暗示水不肯待在河道里。

items.en: The prefix is read either as intensive 'very much' or as separative 'away, over the edge'. Scholars disagree, so the exact force is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个前缀或读作加强义“非常”，或读作分离义“离开、越过边缘”。学界有分歧，确切作用存疑。

items.en: To overflow, to abound, to be rich in something. The subject is always a supply that exceeds its container.
items.cn: 溢出、充盈、富于某物。主语总是一种超出容器的供给。

items.en: Fullness, plenty, riches. The abstract noun turns the overflowing event into a standing condition.
items.cn: 充满、充裕、财富。这个抽象名词把“溢出”的事件变成一种持续状态。

items.en: Old French abondance keeps both the material and the rhetorical senses; English borrows it in the 14c and later adds the scientific counts.
items.cn: 古法语 abondance 同时保留物质义与修辞义；英语 14 世纪借入，后来才添上科学计数的用法。

note.en: The first group is the abundance family, with one word that shares the water root but not the prefix; the second ranks the near-synonyms by what kind of plenty they name.
note.cn: 第一组是 abundance 词族，其中一词共享“水”词根但前缀不同；第二组按“哪一种充裕”来区分近义词。

entries.definition: existing in large quantities. It describes the thing, while abundance names the quantity itself.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在的；描述事物本身，而 abundance 命名数量。

entries.definition: in large quantities, or extremely clearly, as in 'abundantly clear'.
entries.definitionCN: 大量地；或极其明显地，如 abundantly clear。

entries.definition: an amount so great that it is excessive. The prefix pushes the overflow past the point of usefulness.
entries.definitionCN: 多到过分的量；前缀把“溢出”推到超出有用的程度。

entries.definition: to flood. It shares undare with abundance but takes in- 'into', so it means covering, not overflowing with plenty.
entries.definitionCN: 淹没、泛滥。它与 abundance 共享 undare，但用 in-“进入”，意为覆盖，而非“充裕地溢出”。

entries.definition: a sufficient or more than sufficient amount. It is the plain, countable partner of abundance.
entries.definitionCN: 足够或富余的量；是 abundance 平实、可数的伙伴。

entries.definition: an amount so large that it seems poured out. It stresses generosity of quantity more than abundance does.
entries.definitionCN: 多到像倾倒而出的量；比 abundance 更强调数量上的慷慨。

entries.definition: wealth shown in a high standard of living. It covers only the economic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 体现在高生活水平上的财富；只覆盖经济义。

entries.definition: the quality of being plentiful, often used of writing and speech. It suits the style sense.
entries.definitionCN: 丰盛、繁多的性质，常用于文字与言谈；适合“文风”义。

entries.definition: a large stock of money or goods. It names the store, while abundance names the overflowing supply.
entries.definitionCN: 积累的金钱或物资；命名“存货”，而 abundance 命名“溢出的供给”。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: unda 'wave' gives the water image, and ab- is disputed but adds the sense of going beyond. Think of a wave that rises over the bank.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：unda“波浪”提供水的意象，ab- 作用存疑但带来“越过”的意思。想象一道浪涨过河岸。

normal.en: Und- is wave: abundance is water rising until it leaves the riverbed.
normal.cn: und- 是波浪：abundance 就是水涨到离开河床。

normal.en: A full bowl is not abundance until it spills; the extra is the point.
normal.cn: 碗装满还不叫 abundance，要溢出才算；多出来的那点才是关键。

normal.en: In ecology abundance is a head count, so the wave becomes a tally.
normal.cn: 生态学里的 abundance 是一次清点，于是浪变成了计数。

normal.en: Isotope abundance is the same question in fractions: how much of this kind?
normal.cn: 同位素丰度是同一个问题的分数版：这一种占多少？

normal.en: An abundance of caution is a bowl so full that it is hard to carry.
normal.cn: 过度的谨慎，是一只满到不好端的碗。

abstract.en: Abundance is not a number; it is the distance between what is there and what is needed.
abstract.cn: 充裕不是一个数字，而是“已有的”与“所需的”之间的距离。

abstract.en: The same overflow can feed a town or flood it.
abstract.cn: 同一次溢出，可以养活一座城，也可以淹掉它。

abstract.en: Every abundance is measured against a container someone else chose.
abstract.cn: 每一种充裕，都是相对别人选定的那只容器来量的。

examples.en: There is an abundance of cheap labour in the region.
examples.cn: 该地区劳动力充裕而廉价。

examples.en: The reef supports an abundance of fish species.
examples.cn: 这片礁石养育着大量鱼类。

examples.en: He grew up in abundance and never learned to budget.
examples.cn: 他在富足中长大，从没学会做预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，帮 dance”——东西多到能开一场舞会 → abundance 充裕、丰富

root: 源自拉丁语 abundare“溢出、充盈”，由 unda“波浪”加 ab-（作用存疑）构成，本义“像水一样漫出容器”；核心是“多到越过需要的那条边”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abundance, one movement: supply rising past the line of need. The line may be a household budget, a quadrat, a spectrometer reading, a page, a heart, or a market.
sensesIntro.cn: abundance 的八个义项只有一个动作：供给涨过“需要”这条线。这条线可以是家庭预算、样方、光谱读数、一页纸、一颗心，或一个市场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl of water rising until it spills over the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一碗水不断上涨，直到越过碗沿漫出来。

chain: ENGLISH: MORE THAN ENOUGH, THEN WEALTH AND RICHNESS

branches.en: SUPPLY FROM TWO SIDES: a welcome plenty and an unwelcome excess are the same tide, read above or below the rim.
branches.cn: 供给的两面：受欢迎的充裕与不受欢迎的过剩，是同一道潮，只是从碗沿上方或下方去读。

branches.en: RESOURCES: household wealth and the economics of plenty versus scarcity both ask how much a society holds.
branches.cn: 资源：家庭财富与“丰裕对稀缺”的经济学，都在问一个社会握有多少。

branches.en: COUNTING NATURE: species numbers and isotope ratios turn the overflow into a measured share.
branches.cn: 数自然：物种个体数与同位素比值，把“溢出”变成可测的份额。

branches.en: RICHNESS OF FORM: a page or a style can hold more detail than the eye can take in.
branches.cn: 形式的丰盛：一页纸或一种风格，可以容纳眼睛接不住的细节。

branches.en: OVERFLOW OF FEELING: warmth or joy that exceeds the person holding it.
branches.cn: 情感的溢出：超出承载者的温情或喜悦。

intro.en: Abundance is a Latin-derived noun. English expands it with -ant, -ly, and the prefixes super- and over-, then uses it in fixed phrases of quantity.
intro.cn: abundance 是拉丁来源的名词。英语用 -ant、-ly 以及前缀 super-、over- 扩展它，并把它放进表示数量的固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain runs unda 'wave', undare 'to flow', abundare 'to overflow', and abundantia 'plenty'. The English adjective abundant replaces -antia with -ant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 unda“波浪”、undare“流动”、abundare“溢出”、abundantia“充裕”。英语形容词 abundant 用 -ant 替换了 -antia。

items.meaning: existing in large quantities
items.meaningCN: 大量存在的（-ant 构成形容词）
items.example: Fish are abundant in the lake.
items.exampleCN: 湖里鱼很多。

items.meaning: in large quantities; very clearly
items.meaningCN: 大量地；极其明显地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The case is abundantly documented.
items.exampleCN: 这个案例有大量文献记录。

items.meaning: to exist in large numbers
items.meaningCN: 大量存在；富于（动词形式，经古法语）
items.example: Rumours abound about the merger.
items.exampleCN: 关于这桩合并的传言很多。

items.meaning: an excessive amount
items.meaningCN: 过多；过剩（super- 表示“在上、超出”）
items.example: A superabundance of rain ruined the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 雨水过多毁了收成。

items.meaning: more than is needed or wanted
items.meaningCN: 过量；过剩（over- 表示“过度”）
items.example: An overabundance of choices can paralyse buyers.
items.exampleCN: 选择过多会让买家无从下手。

items.meaning: several measured quantities, especially in science
items.meaningCN: 多个测得的量，尤用于科学（复数形式）
items.example: The paper compares isotope abundances across sites.
items.exampleCN: 论文比较了各站点的同位素丰度。

items.meaning: in large quantities
items.meaningCN: 大量地；充裕地（固定短语）
items.example: Olives grow in abundance here.
items.exampleCN: 这里橄榄大量生长。

items.meaning: a very large amount of
items.meaningCN: 大量的……（数量短语）
items.example: She brought an abundance of fruit to the party.
items.exampleCN: 她带了一大堆水果去聚会。

items.meaning: with far more care than usual
items.meaningCN: 极其谨慎地（正式习语）
items.example: The bank lent with an abundance of caution.
items.exampleCN: 银行放贷极为谨慎。

items.meaning: the proportion of an isotope occurring in nature
items.meaningCN: 天然丰度（同位素在自然界中的占比）
items.example: Natural abundance of uranium-235 is under one per cent.
items.exampleCN: 铀-235 的天然丰度不足百分之一。

definition_zh: 加速；加速度；进程的加快；提前、催促；跳级、提前完成学业；经济增速回升；（贷款）加速到期条款；（音乐）速度渐快
definition_en: an increase in speed or rate, or the rate at which velocity changes
core_image: 仪表盘上的指针从左向右扫过去，每一秒都比上一秒更靠右。
scene: The car's acceleration pressed us back into our seats.
sceneCN: 这里 acceleration 是「加速」（第 1 个义项）；句意：汽车的加速把我们压回座椅上。场景：高速入口的匝道，油门到底，后背贴住椅背。

senses.title: An increase in speed
senses.titleCN: 加速：越走越快
senses.definition: the process of moving faster, or the amount by which speed increases
senses.definitionCN: 运动变快的过程，或速度增加的量
senses.example: The car's acceleration pressed us back into our seats.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车的加速把我们压回座椅上。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to hasten. Acceleration is first the plain event of something going faster, felt in the body before it is measured.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为“催促、加快”。acceleration 首先就是某物变快这件事，先被身体感到，然后才被测量。

senses.title: Rate of change of velocity
senses.titleCN: 加速度：速度变化的快慢
senses.definition: in physics, the rate at which velocity changes with time, including changes of direction
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中速度随时间变化的比率，也包括方向变化
senses.example: The sensor logged an acceleration of 3 metres per second squared.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器记录到每秒平方三米的加速度。
senses.why: Physics turned the everyday event into a quantity: not how fast, but how fast the fastness changes. The pointer on the dial becomes a derivative.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把日常事件变成量：不是“多快”，而是“快”本身变化得多快。表盘指针成了一个导数。

senses.title: Speeding up of a process
senses.titleCN: 进程加快：事情推进得更急
senses.definition: an increase in the rate at which a process or activity develops
senses.definitionCN: 过程或活动推进速率的提高
senses.example: The acceleration of the approval process cut months off the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 审批流程的加快把工期缩短了几个月。
senses.why: Processes are spoken of as moving, so they can speed up. The metaphor treats time as distance covered.
senses.whyCN: 过程被说成在“行进”，因此可以加速。这个比喻把时间当作被走过的距离。

senses.title: Hastening a timetable
senses.titleCN: 提前：把日期往前挪
senses.definition: the act of making something happen sooner than originally planned
senses.definitionCN: 使某事比原计划更早发生的行为
senses.example: The board called for acceleration of the launch to catch the holiday market.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会要求提前发布，以赶上假日市场。
senses.why: Here acceleration is applied to the calendar rather than to a body: the starting line is moved closer.
senses.whyCN: 这里的加速作用于日历而非物体：起跑线被向前挪近了。

senses.title: Educational advancement
senses.titleCN: 跳级：学业进度被推快
senses.definition: in education, moving a student through the curriculum faster than the standard pace
senses.definitionCN: 教育中让学生以快于常规的速度完成课程
senses.example: Acceleration let her finish high school a year early.
senses.exampleCN: 跳级让她提前一年读完高中。
senses.why: A student is imagined as moving through school at a speed. To accelerate is to shorten the time spent at each stage.
senses.whyCN: 学生被想象成以某个速度穿过学校。加速就是缩短在每一段停留的时间。

senses.title: Economic growth pickup
senses.titleCN: 增速回升：经济跑得比前一季快
senses.definition: in economics, an increase in the rate of growth of output or activity
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中产出或活动增长率的提高
senses.example: The report showed an acceleration of growth in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 报告显示第二季度增长加快。
senses.why: Economists measure the economy's speed the way drivers measure a car's. Growth that was slowing and now rises is an acceleration.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家量经济的速度，就像司机量车的速度。原本在放缓的增长重新上扬，就是加速。

senses.title: Acceleration clause in finance
senses.titleCN: 加速到期：债务被要求立刻还清
senses.definition: a loan term allowing the lender to demand full repayment immediately if certain conditions are broken
senses.definitionCN: 贷款条款：若违反某些条件，贷款人可要求立即全额偿还
senses.example: Missing two payments triggered the acceleration clause.
senses.exampleCN: 两次未还款触发了加速到期条款。
senses.why: The deadline itself is accelerated: what was spread over years is pulled into the present. The same word for speeding up a process is applied to a payment schedule.
senses.whyCN: 被加速的是期限本身：原本摊在多年里的款项被拉到眼前。同一个“加快进程”的词，用在了还款计划上。

senses.title: Increase of musical tempo
senses.titleCN: 渐快：节拍一点点赶上去
senses.definition: in music, a gradual increase in tempo, often notated as accelerando
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中节拍的逐渐加快，常记作 accelerando
senses.example: The strings begin an acceleration that carries the finale forward.
senses.exampleCN: 弦乐开始渐快，把终曲一路推向前。
senses.why: Music already borrows the language of speed: a passage can be fast or slow, so it can also accelerate. The Italian accelerando is the same Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 音乐本就借用速度的语言：一段音乐可快可慢，因此也能“加速”。意大利语 accelerando 就是同一个拉丁动词。

intro.en: Acceleration is the English noun from Latin acceleratio, built on accelerare 'to hasten', which joins ad- 'to' with celer 'swift'. It entered English in the 17c with the new science of motion.
intro.cn: acceleration 是英语名词，来自拉丁语 acceleratio，由 accelerare“催促、加快”构成，而后者是 ad-“向”加 celer“迅捷”。它随 17 世纪的新运动学进入英语。

items.en: Swift, quick. It is the source of celerity and of the scientific term, and it describes speed itself rather than the act of increasing it.
items.cn: 迅捷、快速。它是 celerity 与这个科学术语的来源，描述“速度快”本身，而不是“使速度增加”的动作。

items.en: To, toward. Attached to a verb it points the action at a goal, here at a higher speed.
items.cn: 向、朝。加在动词前，把动作指向某个目标，这里指向更高的速度。

items.en: To hasten, to quicken, to bring forward. Latin used it of both speed and time, which is why English later applies it to schedules.
items.cn: 催促、加快、提前。拉丁语既用它说速度，也用它说时间，所以英语后来能拿它说日程。

items.en: A hastening. The -io noun names the action, not yet a measured physical quantity.
items.cn: 加快、催促。-io 名词命名动作，当时还不是一个被测的物理量。

items.en: English borrows the noun as mechanics takes shape. Galileo and Newton had made change of velocity a quantity, and the word settles into that role.
items.cn: 英语在力学成形时借入这个名词。伽利略与牛顿已把速度变化变成可测的量，这个词就此固定在那个位置上。

items.en: From physics the word spreads to timetables, schooling, economics, contracts, and music. Each extension keeps the same shape: a rate that is itself rising.
items.cn: 从物理学出发，这个词扩散到日程、教育、经济、合同与音乐。每次延伸都保持同一形状：一个本身在上升的速率。

note.en: The first group is the acceleration family plus a famous look-alike from a different root; the second separates speed, rate, and mere hastening.
note.cn: 第一组是 acceleration 词族，外加一个来自不同词根的著名形近词；第二组把“速度”“速率”和“单纯催促”分开。

entries.definition: to go faster or to make something go faster. It is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 加速；使加速；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: something that increases speed, such as a pedal or a particle machine.
entries.definitionCN: 增加速度的东西，如油门踏板或粒子加速器。

entries.definition: tending to speed something up. It describes the tendency rather than the measured change.
entries.definitionCN: 有加速倾向的；描述倾向而非测得的改变。

entries.definition: fame or a famous person. It comes from Latin celeber 'frequented, famous', not from celer 'swift', so the similarity is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名声或名人。它来自拉丁语 celeber“人多去的、著名的”，而非 celer“迅捷”，相似只在拼写。

entries.definition: an increase in speed or rate. It is the everyday word, without the technical precision of acceleration.
entries.definitionCN: 速度或速率的提高；日常说法，没有 acceleration 的技术精确度。

entries.definition: the act of making something happen sooner. It fits the timetable sense better than the physics sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事更早发生；更贴合“日程”义而非物理义。

entries.definition: a becoming quicker, often of a natural process or of rhythm. It carries a softer, more organic tone.
entries.definitionCN: 变快，常用于自然过程或节奏；语气更柔和、更有生命感。

entries.definition: an increase in strength or force rather than in speed. It covers cases where acceleration is figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 强度或力度的增加，而非速度；覆盖 acceleration 的比喻用法。

entries.definition: forward progress in a career, a cause, or a course of study. It suits the educational sense.
entries.definitionCN: 事业、事业或学业上的推进；适合“教育”义。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ad- 'to' plus celer 'swift' gives accelerare 'to hasten'. Celer also survives in celerity, and it has nothing to do with celebrity.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ad-“向”加 celer“迅捷”得到 accelerare“加快”。celer 也留在 celerity 里，它与 celebrity 无关。

normal.en: Celer means swift: accelerate is to send something toward swiftness.
normal.cn: celer 意为迅捷：accelerate 就是把某物推向迅捷。

normal.en: Speed is how fast you go; acceleration is how fast that changes.
normal.cn: 速度是你走多快；加速度是“这个快”变化多快。

normal.en: A timetable can accelerate because Latin used the verb for time as well as motion.
normal.cn: 日程也能 accelerate，因为拉丁语这个词既用于时间也用于运动。

normal.en: A student who accelerates skips a stage; a borrower who accelerates pays years in one day.
normal.cn: 跳级的学生省掉一段；触发加速条款的借款人把几年压成一天。

normal.en: Celebrity is from celeber 'frequented', so fame does not make you faster.
normal.cn: celebrity 来自 celeber“人多去的”，所以名气并不会让你更快。

abstract.en: Acceleration is the second derivative of position: the shape of a journey, not its length.
abstract.cn: 加速度是位置对时间的二阶导数：是旅程的形状，不是旅程的长度。

abstract.en: Anything with a rate can be accelerated, including trust and inflation.
abstract.cn: 任何有速率的东西都能被加速，包括信任与通胀。

abstract.en: To accelerate is always to shorten something, even when nothing moves.
abstract.cn: 加速总是在缩短某样东西，即使没有任何物体在移动。

examples.en: The train's smooth acceleration surprised the passengers.
examples.cn: 列车平稳的加速让乘客惊讶。

examples.en: Newton defined force as mass times acceleration.
examples.cn: 牛顿把力定义为质量乘以加速度。

examples.en: They agreed to an acceleration of the payment schedule.
examples.cn: 他们同意提前还款计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，塞了，来神”——堵车时一脚油门，车突然窜出去 → acceleration 加速

root: 源自拉丁语 accelerare“加快”，由 ad-“向”+ celer“迅捷”构成，名词 acceleratio 加了 -io；核心是“速率本身在上升”，而不是“已经很快”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acceleration, one shape: a rate that rises. It can be a car's speed, a derivative in physics, a process, a calendar, a school year, an economy, a debt schedule, or a tempo.
sensesIntro.cn: acceleration 的八个义项只有一个形状：一个正在上升的速率。它可以是车速、物理导数、流程、日历、学年、经济、还款计划，或节拍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial whose needle moves further right every second.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只表盘的指针，每一秒都往右多走一点。

chain: ENGLISH 17c: A MEASURED CHANGE OF VELOCITY
ANY RATE THAT IS ITSELF RISING

branches.en: MOTION: the felt push in the back and the number on the dial are the same event, one lived and one measured.
branches.cn: 运动：后背感到的推力和表盘上的数字是同一件事，一个被体验，一个被测量。

branches.en: TIME COMPRESSED: a process, a launch date, and an economy all move through time, so all three can run faster.
branches.cn: 被压缩的时间：流程、发布日、经济都在时间中行进，因此三者都能跑得更快。

branches.en: SCHOOLING: a student is imagined as travelling through the curriculum, so a stage can be skipped.
branches.cn: 学业：学生被想象成穿过课程，因此可以跳过一段。

branches.en: DEBT: the payment calendar is pulled forward until years become due now.
branches.cn: 债务：还款日历被向前拉，直到几年后的款项变成现在到期。

branches.en: MUSIC: tempo is a speed, so a passage can press ahead.
branches.cn: 音乐：节拍就是一种速度，因此一段音乐可以往前赶。

intro.en: Acceleration is a Latin -io noun. English builds the verb with -ate, the agent noun with -or, the adjective with -ive, and pairs it with technical nouns.
intro.cn: acceleration 是拉丁语 -io 名词。英语用 -ate 造动词、-or 造施事名词、-ive 造形容词，并与技术名词搭配。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is celer 'swift', accelerare 'to hasten', and acceleratio 'a hastening'. The prefix ad- assimilates to ac- before c.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 celer“迅捷”、accelerare“加快”、acceleratio“加快”。前缀 ad- 在 c 前同化为 ac-。

items.meaning: to go or make something go faster
items.meaningCN: 加速；使加速（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The government hopes to accelerate the transition.
items.exampleCN: 政府希望加快转型。

items.meaning: a device or pedal that increases speed
items.meaningCN: 加速器；油门（-or 构成施事名词）
items.example: He put his foot on the accelerator.
items.exampleCN: 他踩下油门。

items.meaning: having the tendency to speed something up
items.meaningCN: 有加速作用的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The policy had an accelerative effect on investment.
items.exampleCN: 该政策对投资有加速作用。

items.meaning: made faster or completed in less time
items.meaningCN: 加速的；速成的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: She joined an accelerated degree programme.
items.exampleCN: 她参加了速成学位项目。

items.meaning: a decrease in speed
items.meaningCN: 减速（de- 表示“向下、减少”）
items.example: The bus made a gentle deceleration at the stop.
items.exampleCN: 公交车在站台缓缓减速。

items.meaning: a road lane used to reach highway speed
items.meaningCN: 加速车道（用于并入高速前提速的车道）
items.example: Use the acceleration lane to match the traffic speed.
items.exampleCN: 利用加速车道赶上交通流速。

items.meaning: acceleration that does not change with time
items.meaningCN: 匀加速度（物理术语，加速度不随时间变化）
items.example: Under constant acceleration, distance grows with the square of time.
items.exampleCN: 在匀加速下，距离随时间平方增长。

items.meaning: the acceleration produced by gravity
items.meaningCN: 重力加速度（物理术语）
items.example: Gravitational acceleration on Earth is about 9.8 m/s².
items.exampleCN: 地球上的重力加速度约为 9.8 米/秒²。

items.meaning: a loan term making the whole debt due at once
items.meaningCN: 加速到期条款（使全部债务立即到期的贷款条款）
items.example: The acceleration clause was invoked after the default.
items.exampleCN: 违约后触发了加速到期条款。

items.meaning: an increase in the rate of economic growth
items.meaningCN: 增长加快（经济学术语）
items.example: The figures point to an acceleration of growth.
items.exampleCN: 数据表明增长正在加快。

definition_zh: 配饰；附件；附加设备；（法律）从犯、帮凶；（生物）附属的（器官、神经）；（建筑）附属的；装饰物；（法律）事后从犯；附加的、补充的
definition_en: an extra item that adds to something, a decorative item, or a person who helps in a crime
core_image: 一只手提包旁边挂着一条丝巾，包本身能用，丝巾让它完整。
scene: She matched a silk scarf to her outfit as the final accessory.
sceneCN: 这里 accessory 是「配饰」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她配了一条丝巾作为最后的配饰。场景：出门前在镜子前系上围巾，衣服本身已穿好。

derivatives.zh: 配有饰物的；加装附件的

senses.title: Fashion accessory
senses.titleCN: 配饰：让整套穿戴收尾的小物
senses.definition: an item such as a scarf, belt, or jewellery worn to complete or decorate an outfit
senses.definitionCN: 围巾、腰带、首饰等用来收尾或装饰整套衣着的物品
senses.example: She matched a silk scarf to her outfit as the final accessory.
senses.exampleCN: 她配了一条丝巾作为最后的配饰。
senses.why: The Latin source means something that comes alongside. A scarf comes alongside the coat: the coat works without it, but the look is unfinished.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为“从旁边过来之物”。丝巾从大衣旁边来：大衣不配它也成立，但整体造型没收尾。

senses.title: Add-on device or attachment
senses.titleCN: 配件：主机之外补上的那件
senses.definition: an extra device or part that is attached to a main machine to extend what it can do
senses.definitionCN: 附接到主机上以扩展功能的额外装置或部件
senses.example: The camera comes with a strap and two other accessories.
senses.exampleCN: 相机附带一条背带和另外两件配件。
senses.why: The item is added to a host object, exactly as the Latin verb meant 'to come to'. It does not replace the host; it extends it.
senses.whyCN: 该物被加到主机上，正是拉丁动词“来到、附加”的意思。它不替换主机，而是扩展主机。

senses.title: Accessory to a crime
senses.titleCN: 从犯：没动手，但从旁帮了
senses.definition: a person who helps another commit or plan a crime without being the principal offender
senses.definitionCN: 帮助他人实施或策划犯罪、但本身不是主犯的人
senses.example: He was charged as an accessory to the robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控为抢劫案从犯。
senses.why: The legal sense is the oldest in English. The helper stands beside the doer, present and contributing, but not the hand that acts.
senses.whyCN: 法律义是英语中最早的用法。帮助者站在实施者身旁，在场、有贡献，但不是那只动手的手。

senses.title: Accessory organ or nerve
senses.titleCN: 附属结构：不主事但不可少
senses.definition: in anatomy, a structure that supports or assists a main organ, such as the accessory nerve
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中支持或辅助主要器官的结构，如副神经
senses.example: Damage to the accessory nerve can limit shoulder movement.
senses.exampleCN: 副神经受损会限制肩部活动。
senses.why: Anatomy uses the word for parts that assist rather than lead. The structure is not the main organ, but the organ works worse without it.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学用它指辅助而非主导的部分。它不是主器官，但缺了它，主器官就运作得更差。

senses.title: Accessory building
senses.titleCN: 附属建筑：主屋旁的小屋
senses.definition: in architecture and planning, a secondary structure on the same lot as a main building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与规划中，与主建筑位于同一地块的次要建筑
senses.example: The garage is a lawful accessory building to the house.
senses.exampleCN: 车库是这栋住宅合法的附属建筑。
senses.why: A shed or garage stands beside the house and serves it. Planning law borrows the social relation of helper and principal.
senses.whyCN: 棚屋或车库立在住宅旁并服务于它。规划法借用了“辅助者与主体”的社会关系。

senses.title: Ornament or adornment
senses.titleCN: 装饰：只为了好看的那一层
senses.definition: something added purely for decoration rather than for use
senses.definitionCN: 纯粹为装饰而非为实用而添加的东西
senses.example: The carved brackets are an accessory, not a support.
senses.exampleCN: 那些雕花托架是装饰，不是承重构件。
senses.why: Here the alongside-item has no function at all. It is the pure decorative residue of the fashion sense, separated from clothing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“旁加之物”完全没有功能。它是“配饰”义剥离衣着之后的纯装饰残余。

senses.title: Accessory after the fact
senses.titleCN: 事后从犯：事成之后才帮忙
senses.definition: a person who helps an offender avoid arrest or punishment after the crime has been committed
senses.definitionCN: 犯罪完成后帮助犯罪人逃避逮捕或处罚的人
senses.example: Hiding the getaway car made her an accessory after the fact.
senses.exampleCN: 藏起逃逸车辆使她成为事后从犯。
senses.why: The timeline splits the legal sense. Help before or during the crime makes an accessory before the fact; help afterwards gets its own label.
senses.whyCN: 时间线把法律义切开。犯罪前或犯罪中帮忙是“事前从犯”；事成之后帮忙另有名称。

senses.title: Supplementary, as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 附加的：形容词用法
senses.definition: used as an adjective, adding to or supporting something else rather than being essential
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时，表示补充或辅助某物，而非必不可少
senses.example: The clause has an accessory function in the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款在合同中起附加作用。
senses.why: The noun's meaning thins into a modifier: 'of the nature of an accessory'. English frequently lets a noun work as an adjective without change.
senses.whyCN: 名词义淡化为修饰语：“具有附属性质的”。英语常让名词不加变化就作形容词。

intro.en: Accessory comes from Latin accessorius, 'that which comes to or beside', from accedere 'to approach, be added', itself ad- 'to' plus cedere 'to go'. English took it first as a legal term in the 17c.
intro.cn: accessory 来自拉丁语 accessorius“从旁边来到的”，源于 accedere“靠近、附加”，即 ad-“向”加 cedere“走”。英语 17 世纪先把它当法律术语借入。

items.en: To go, yield, or withdraw. It supplies the motion inside accedere and also underlies proceed, concede, and exceed.
items.cn: 走、让、退去。它为 accedere 提供“移动”，也是 proceed、concede、exceed 的词根。

items.en: To, toward. Before c it assimilates and becomes ac-, which is why the word is accedere and not adcedere.
items.cn: 向、朝。在 c 前同化为 ac-，所以是 accedere 而不是 adcedere。

items.en: To come near, to be added to. The image is a person or thing walking up to a group and joining it.
items.cn: 靠近、被加到。画面是一个人或有物走到一群旁边并加入其中。

items.en: An adjective meaning 'that which comes beside'. In law it described a person or thing attached to a principal case.
items.cn: 形容词，意为“从旁边而来的”。在法律中，它指附属于主案的人或物。

items.en: English borrows it as a legal noun: an accessory to a crime. The spelling accessary was common for the person, and both survive.
items.cn: 英语把它作为法律名词借入：犯罪从犯。指人时旧拼法 accessary 很常见，两种拼法都留存至今。

items.en: The word spreads from the courtroom to dress, then to machines. The fashion sense appears in the 18c, the device sense in the 20c.
items.cn: 这个词从法庭扩散到衣饰，再到机器。时尚义出现在 18 世纪，设备义在 20 世纪。

note.en: The first group is the accessory family, including the old legal spelling and a verb; the second sorts the near-synonyms by whether the added thing is useful, decorative, or criminal.
note.cn: 第一组是 accessory 词族，含旧法律拼法与一个动词；第二组按“所加之物是有用、装饰还是涉案”来区分近义词。

entries.definition: the older spelling for a person who assists in a crime. Modern usage usually prefers accessory for both noun senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指犯罪帮凶的旧拼法；现代用法通常两种名词义都用 accessory。

entries.definition: to add decorative items to an outfit or a room. It turns the fashion sense into an action.
entries.definitionCN: 给衣着或房间添加饰物；把“时尚配饰”义变成动作。

entries.definition: of or like an accessory; supplementary. It is the formal adjective beside the everyday accessory.
entries.definitionCN: 附属的、附加的；是日常 accessory 旁边的正式形容词。

entries.definition: the right or means to enter or use something. It shares accedere but names entry, not the thing that comes alongside.
entries.definitionCN: 进入或使用的权利或途径；共享 accedere，但命名“进入”，而非“从旁而来之物”。

entries.definition: a part fixed to a main object to extend it. It suits the device sense and implies a physical join.
entries.definitionCN: 固定在主体上以扩展功能的部件；适合设备义，含物理连接之意。

entries.definition: something added to a main thing but not essential to it. It is the most formal match for the supplementary sense.
entries.definitionCN: 加于主体但非必需之物；最贴合“附加”义的正式词。

entries.definition: an extra item bought to go with a main product. It is the shop-counter word for the device sense.
entries.definitionCN: 随主产品购买的额外物件；设备义的柜台口语。

entries.definition: an ornament that makes something more attractive. It covers only the decorative senses, with no legal or mechanical use.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更美的装饰物；只覆盖装饰义，不含法律或机械用法。

entries.definition: a person who helps commit a crime, often more actively than an accessory. It is the near neighbour of the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助实施犯罪的人，通常比 accessory 更主动；是法律义的近邻。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ad- 'to' plus cedere 'go' gives accedere 'come near'; accessorius is 'the thing that comes alongside'. The double c is assimilation, not a prefix of its own.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ad-“向”加 cedere“走”得到 accedere“靠近”；accessorius 就是“从旁边来的东西”。双写 c 是同化，不是独立前缀。

normal.en: Cedere means go: an accessory is whatever walks up beside the main thing.
normal.cn: cedere 意为走：accessory 就是走到主体旁边的那件东西。

normal.en: A scarf beside a coat, a lens beside a camera, a shed beside a house: all come alongside.
normal.cn: 大衣旁的丝巾、相机旁的镜头、住宅旁的棚屋：都从旁边来。

normal.en: In law the one who stands beside the doer is an accessory, not the hand that acts.
normal.cn: 在法律中，站在实施者旁边的人是从犯，而不是动手的那只手。

normal.en: After the fact, the help comes too late to be part of the crime, so it gets its own name.
normal.cn: 事成之后的帮忙来得太晚，进不了犯罪本身，于是另有名称。

normal.en: Access means entry; accessory means the thing that came in alongside.
normal.cn: access 是“进入”；accessory 是“跟着进来、待在旁边的那件”。

abstract.en: An accessory is defined by a centre it does not own.
abstract.cn: 配饰由它所不拥有的那个中心来定义。

abstract.en: The same word can decorate a wrist and convict a accomplice, because both mean 'beside'.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能装饰手腕，也能给人定罪，因为两者都意为“在旁边”。

abstract.en: Nothing essential, everything decisive: that is the accessory's paradox.
abstract.cn: 并非必需，却往往决定成败：这就是附属之物的悖论。

examples.en: Belt and earrings were the only accessories she wore.
examples.cn: 她只戴了腰带和耳环这两件配饰。

examples.en: The tablet needs a keyboard accessory for long documents.
examples.cn: 这款平板需要键盘配件来处理长文档。

examples.en: The court found him an accessory to the fraud.
examples.cn: 法庭认定他是该欺诈案的从犯。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，塞手里”——出门前把丝巾塞到手里当配饰 → accessory 配饰、附件

root: 源自拉丁语 accessorius“从旁边来到的”，由 ad-“向”+ cedere“走”构成的 accedere“靠近、附加”派生；核心是“不是主体，从旁边补上来”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accessory, one position: beside. Beside a coat, a camera, a house, a nerve, a crime, or a clause — the accessory is defined by the main thing it never replaces.
sensesIntro.cn: accessory 的八个义项只有一个位置：在旁边。在大衣、相机、住宅、神经、案件或条款旁边——附属物始终由那个它从不取代的主体来定义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scarf hung beside a finished outfit, completing it without being part of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条丝巾挂在已穿好的衣服旁，让它完整，却不属于它。

chain: AD- + CEDERE = ACCEDERE, TO COME NEAR
ENGLISH 17c: LEGAL HELPER IN A CRIME
ENGLISH 20c: DEVICE ADDED TO A MACHINE

branches.en: DECORATION: a scarf and a carved bracket both come alongside for looks alone.
branches.cn: 装饰：丝巾与雕花托架都只为好看而从旁边加上。

branches.en: SUPPLEMENT: a camera accessory and an accessory clause extend a main thing without replacing it.
branches.cn: 补充：相机配件与附加条款扩展主体，而不取代主体。

branches.en: COMPLICITY: helping before or after the crime puts a person beside the offender, on a different timetable.
branches.cn: 同谋：犯罪前或犯罪后帮忙，都把人放到罪犯旁边，只是时间表不同。

branches.en: ANATOMY: a nerve that assists a main organ plays the same supporting role inside the body.
branches.cn: 解剖：辅助主器官的神经，在身体内部扮演同样的支持角色。

branches.en: BUILDINGS: a garage on the same lot stands beside the house as helper to principal.
branches.cn: 建筑：同一地块上的车库立在住宅旁，如辅助者之于主体。

intro.en: Accessory is a Latin-derived noun and adjective. English adds -ize for the verb, -ial for a formal adjective, and keeps the old -ary spelling for the legal person.
intro.cn: accessory 是拉丁来源的名词与形容词。英语加 -ize 造动词、-ial 造正式形容词，并保留旧 -ary 拼法指法律上的人。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is cedere 'to go', accedere 'to come near', and accessorius 'coming beside'. The prefix ad- becomes ac- before c.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 cedere“走”、accedere“靠近”、accessorius“从旁而来”。前缀 ad- 在 c 前变为 ac-。

items.meaning: to add decorative accessories
items.meaningCN: 用配饰装扮；加配件（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: She accessorized the dress with a wide belt.
items.exampleCN: 她用一条宽腰带搭配这条裙子。

items.meaning: fitted out with accessories
items.meaningCN: 配有饰物或附件的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: The car is fully accessorized for winter.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车为冬季配齐了附件。

items.meaning: supplementary, of the nature of an accessory
items.meaningCN: 附属的、附加的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The court treated the payment as accessorial.
items.exampleCN: 法庭将该笔付款视为附加性质。

items.meaning: a person who assists in a crime
items.meaningCN: 从犯（旧拼法，多指人）
items.example: The old statute uses the spelling accessary.
items.exampleCN: 旧法规使用 accessary 这一拼法。

items.meaning: a decorative item worn with clothes
items.meaningCN: 时尚配饰（名词复合）
items.example: Sunglasses became a fashion accessory in the 20c.
items.exampleCN: 太阳镜在 20 世纪成了时尚配饰。

items.meaning: add-on items sold for a phone
items.meaningCN: 手机配件（名词复数搭配）
items.example: The shop sells cases, chargers, and other phone accessories.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖手机壳、充电器等配件。

items.meaning: a secondary structure on the same lot
items.meaningCN: 附属建筑（同一地块上的次要建筑）
items.example: A permit is needed for any accessory building.
items.exampleCN: 任何附属建筑都需要许可。

items.meaning: the eleventh cranial nerve
items.meaningCN: 副神经（第十一对脑神经）
items.example: The accessory nerve controls part of the trapezius.
items.exampleCN: 副神经控制斜方肌的一部分。

items.meaning: one who helps an offender after the crime
items.meaningCN: 事后从犯（犯罪后帮助罪犯者）
items.example: He was convicted as an accessory after the fact.
items.exampleCN: 他被判为事后从犯。

items.meaning: a helper in a specified crime
items.meaningCN: ……的从犯（法律搭配框架）
items.example: She was accused as an accessory to the conspiracy.
items.exampleCN: 她被控为该阴谋的从犯。

definition_zh: 称赞；欢呼；公开赞扬；喝彩；（以掌声或呼声）宣告；评论界的赞誉；公认；拥立、欢呼致意
definition_en: to praise something enthusiastically and publicly, or such praise itself
core_image: 剧场灯光亮起，全场起立，掌声像一波浪推向舞台。
scene: Her first novel won critical acclaim across Europe.
sceneCN: 这里 acclaim 是「评论界的赞誉」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她的第一部小说在欧洲赢得评论界赞誉。场景：报纸文化版的整版书评，标题都在夸。

derivatives.zh: 未获赞誉的；无人喝彩的

senses.title: To praise enthusiastically
senses.titleCN: 称赞：大声说好
senses.definition: to praise someone or something with strong, public enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 以强烈而公开的热情赞扬某人或某物
senses.example: Critics acclaimed the film for its restraint.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人称赞这部电影的克制。
senses.why: The Latin verb is to shout to. To acclaim is not to approve quietly but to send approval outward with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为“向……呼喊”。acclaim 不是默默认可，而是用声音把赞许送出去。

senses.title: Public praise as a noun
senses.titleCN: 赞誉：喊出来的名声
senses.definition: enthusiastic and public praise, especially in the arts
senses.definitionCN: 热情而公开的赞扬，尤指文艺领域
senses.example: The album received acclaim from both fans and critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑受到歌迷与评论家的赞誉。
senses.why: The noun is the shout detached from the moment of shouting. It becomes a quantity of reputation that a work can win or lack.
senses.whyCN: 名词是“喊声”脱离呼喊瞬间后的沉淀。它变成一种名声的量，作品可以赢得它，也可以没有。

senses.title: To declare by acclamation
senses.titleCN: 以欢呼通过：不用投票就定了
senses.definition: to approve or elect someone by a show of voices rather than by a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 以呼声而非正式投票来通过或选举某人
senses.example: The delegates acclaimed her as the new chair.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们以欢呼拥立她为新任主席。
senses.why: In an assembly, enough voices at once can stand in for a count. Acclaim here is a decision made by volume.
senses.whyCN: 在集会上，足够多同时发出的声音可以替代计票。这里的 acclaim 是用音量做出的决定。

senses.title: Critical acclaim
senses.titleCN: 评论界赞誉：专业读者的集体肯定
senses.definition: approval from reviewers and specialists, often contrasted with popular success
senses.definitionCN: 来自评论者与专业同行的认可，常与大众成功相对
senses.example: Her first novel won critical acclaim across Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在欧洲赢得评论界赞誉。
senses.why: Modern usage separates the shouting crowd into two: the critics and the public. Critical acclaim is the approval of those whose job is to judge.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把呼喊的人群分成两拨：评论者与公众。critical acclaim 是“以判断为职业的人”的认可。

senses.title: To applaud or approve vocally
senses.titleCN: 喝彩：用掌声和喊声表态
senses.definition: to show approval by clapping, cheering, or shouting together
senses.definitionCN: 以鼓掌、欢呼或齐声呼喊表示赞许
senses.example: The crowd acclaimed the goal as the whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声响起时，人群为这粒进球欢呼。
senses.why: This sense keeps the body in the word: acclaim is audible approval, not a written verdict.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把身体留在词里：acclaim 是听得见的认可，而不是书面裁决。

senses.title: Widespread recognition
senses.titleCN: 公认：名声扩散到很远
senses.definition: general recognition of excellence over a wide public
senses.definitionCN: 卓越之处在广泛公众中获得普遍承认
senses.example: The design has gained international acclaim.
senses.exampleCN: 这项设计获得了国际声誉。
senses.why: When praise travels beyond the room where it began, it becomes recognition. The shout turns into a reputation.
senses.whyCN: 当赞誉走出最初那个房间，它就成了“公认”。喊声变成了名声。

senses.title: To hail a winner
senses.titleCN: 欢呼致意：把胜者迎上台
senses.definition: to greet a victor or a newly arrived hero with cheers
senses.definitionCN: 以欢呼迎接胜利者或新到场的英雄
senses.example: The team was acclaimed by thousands at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在机场受到数千人欢呼迎接。
senses.why: The direction of the shout is outward toward a person. Hailing a winner is acclaim with a destination.
senses.whyCN: 喊声朝外指向某个人。为胜者欢呼，就是有明确接收者的 acclaim。

senses.title: Unison shout of approval
senses.titleCN: 齐声叫好：许多声音合成一个
senses.definition: a collective shout of agreement or joy from many voices at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多声音同时发出的赞同或喜悦的呼喊
senses.example: A single acclaim rose from the terraces when the runner appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 跑者出现时，看台上升起一片齐声欢呼。
senses.why: At its most literal, acclaim is a sound made by many mouths at one moment. The word's oldest layer is simply noise in agreement.
senses.whyCN: 最字面地说，acclaim 是许多张嘴在同一刻发出的声音。这个词最古老的一层，就是表示赞同的噪音。

intro.en: Acclaim comes from Latin acclamare, 'to shout at', from ad- 'to' plus clamare 'to shout'. The noun acclamatio passed through French into English in the 17c.
intro.cn: acclaim 来自拉丁语 acclamare“向……呼喊”，即 ad-“向”加 clamare“喊”。名词 acclamatio 经法语在 17 世纪进入英语。

items.en: To shout, cry out, call. It is the source of exclaim, proclaim, and clamour, and it always involves a voice raised.
items.cn: 喊、叫、呼。它是 exclaim、proclaim、clamour 的来源，总含“提高声音”之意。

items.en: To, toward. Before c it becomes ac-, so the verb is acclamare: to shout in the direction of someone.
items.cn: 向、朝。在 c 前变为 ac-，所以动词是 acclamare：朝某人喊。

items.en: To shout to, to call out in approval or greeting. Roman assemblies used it of crowds hailing a general or a candidate.
items.cn: 向……呼喊，以赞许或问候呼叫。罗马集会用它指人群向将军或候选人欢呼。

items.en: A shout of approval, a public demonstration of consent. The noun could mean both a cheer and a formal show of voices.
items.cn: 赞许的呼喊、公开表示同意。这个名词既可指喝彩，也可指正式的呼声表决。

items.en: French acclamation carries the noun into English. The verb acclaim follows, and by the 18c it is used of critics and audiences.
items.cn: 法语 acclamation 把名词带入英语。动词 acclaim 随后而来，到 18 世纪已用于评论者与观众。

items.en: The word splits into critical acclaim and popular acclaim, and the verb extends to approving decisions as well as people.
items.cn: 这个词分化为 critical acclaim 与 popular acclaim，动词也从“赞美人”扩展到“赞许决定”。

note.en: The first group is the acclaim family plus two words that share clamare by other routes; the second ranks praise from the loudest public sound to the quietest recognition.
note.cn: 第一组是 acclaim 词族，外加两个从别的路径共享 clamare 的词；第二组按“从最响的公众声音到最静的认可”排列近义词。

entries.definition: a shout of approval, or a vote carried by voices. It names the event that acclaim names as a state.
entries.definitionCN: 赞许的呼喊，或以呼声通过的表决；命名 acclaim 作为状态所命名的事件。

entries.definition: expressing or consisting of acclamation. A formal word, mostly found in descriptions of assemblies.
entries.definitionCN: 表示欢呼的、由欢呼构成的；正式词，多见于对集会的描述。

entries.definition: to assert or demand. It also goes back to clamare, but through Old French clamer 'to call', and it means calling for something, not praising it.
entries.definitionCN: 声称；要求。它同样源于 clamare，但经古法语 clamer“呼喊”，意为“索取”，而非“赞扬”。

entries.definition: to cry out suddenly. It shares clamare but takes ex- 'out', so the voice goes out in surprise, not in praise.
entries.definitionCN: 突然喊出。共享 clamare，但用 ex-“向外”，声音因惊讶而出，不是因赞美而出。

entries.definition: the expression of approval or admiration. It is the neutral word and needs no audience.
entries.definitionCN: 表达赞许或钦佩；是中性的词，不需要听众。

entries.definition: approval shown by clapping. It is the physical sound that acclaim often accompanies.
entries.definitionCN: 以鼓掌表示的赞许；是 acclaim 常伴随的物理声响。

entries.definition: statements of praise, usually from many people. It is the literary plural for a body of acclaim.
entries.definitionCN: 众人的赞扬，常为文学用语；是“一片赞誉”的文学化复数。

entries.definition: a sustained burst of applause from an audience. It is the loudest form of acclaim in a hall.
entries.definitionCN: 观众经久不息的掌声；是礼堂里最响亮的 acclaim。

entries.definition: public acknowledgement of someone's achievement. It is acclaim after the noise has stopped.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人成就的公开承认；是噪音停止之后的 acclaim。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ad- 'to' plus clamare 'shout'. The same root gives exclaim, proclaim, and clamour; claim is a cousin that travelled through French.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ad-“向”加 clamare“喊”。同一词根给出 exclaim、proclaim、clamour；claim 是经法语走另一条路的亲戚。

normal.en: Clamare means shout: to acclaim is to shout toward someone.
normal.cn: clamare 意为喊：acclaim 就是朝某人喊。

normal.en: Acclaim is praise with a volume knob; praise can be a whisper.
normal.cn: acclaim 是带音量旋钮的赞扬；praise 可以只是耳语。

normal.en: Exclaim goes out in surprise; acclaim goes out in approval. Same shout, different prefix.
normal.cn: exclaim 因惊讶而出，acclaim 因赞许而出。同一喊声，不同前缀。

normal.en: In an assembly, enough voices at once replace the ballot: that is acclamation.
normal.cn: 在集会上，足够多同时发出的声音替代了选票：这就是 acclamation。

normal.en: A film can win acclaim and still lose money; the shout and the ticket are different currencies.
normal.cn: 一部电影可以赢得赞誉却仍然亏钱；喊声与票房是两种货币。

abstract.en: Acclaim is a sound that other people make about you, and it can be withdrawn.
abstract.cn: 赞誉是别人对你发出的声音，而它随时可以被收回。

abstract.en: The same crowd that acclaims a winner can acclaim the next one.
abstract.cn: 为这个胜者欢呼的人群，也能为下一个欢呼。

abstract.en: Every acclaim measures the distance between a work and its moment.
abstract.cn: 每一次赞誉，量的都是一件作品与它那个时代之间的距离。

examples.en: The audience acclaimed the pianist with a long ovation.
examples.cn: 观众以长时间的起立鼓掌向钢琴家致意。

examples.en: Her research was acclaimed as a breakthrough.
examples.cn: 她的研究被赞誉为一项突破。

examples.en: The mayor's decision drew acclaim from local businesses.
examples.cn: 市长的决定受到本地企业的称赞。

dict_mnemonic.text: “啊，claim”——把 claim 大声喊出来，就是公开称赞 → acclaim 欢呼、赞誉

root: 源自拉丁语 acclamare“向……呼喊”，由 ad-“向”+ clamare“喊”构成，名词 acclamatio 经法语入英语；核心是“把赞许喊向某个人”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acclaim, one direction: a voice sent outward in approval. It can be sent to a film, a novel, a winner, a chair, or a decision, and it can settle into reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: acclaim 的八个义项只有一个方向：把赞许的声音向外送出。它可以送给一部电影、一部小说、一位胜者、一位主席或一个决定，也可以沉淀为名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall on its feet, applause pushing toward the stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：全场起立，掌声像浪一样推向舞台。

chain: AD- + CLAMARE = ACCLAMARE, TO SHOUT AT

branches.en: VOICE: to praise and to applaud are the same outward shout, one worded and one sounded.
branches.cn: 声音：赞扬与喝彩是同一次向外的呼喊，一个成为词，一个成为响。

branches.en: REPUTATION: praise that outlives the moment becomes a quantity of public recognition.
branches.cn: 名声：活得比瞬间更久的赞扬，变成一份公众认可的量。

branches.en: HAILING: a vote by voices and a greeting at the airport both direct the shout at a person.
branches.cn: 致意：以呼声表决与在机场迎接，都把喊声指向某个人。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: critical acclaim is the approval of those whose profession is to evaluate.
branches.cn: 判断：评论界赞誉，是以评估为职业的人的认可。

branches.en: UNISON: at its root the word is simply many voices agreeing at once.
branches.cn: 齐声：追到根上，这个词就是许多声音在同一刻表示同意。

intro.en: Acclaim enters English as a verb and a noun. The -ation noun is the Latin action noun, -atory is its adjective, and -ed forms a participle meaning 'praised'.
intro.cn: acclaim 以动词和名词进入英语。-ation 名词是拉丁动作名词，-atory 是它的形容词，-ed 构成表示“受赞誉的”分词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is clamare 'to shout', acclamare 'to shout at', and acclamatio 'a shout of approval'. The prefix ad- becomes ac- before c.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 clamare“喊”、acclamare“向……喊”、acclamatio“赞许的呼喊”。前缀 ad- 在 c 前变为 ac-。

items.meaning: a shout of approval; approval by voices
items.meaningCN: 欢呼；以呼声通过（-ation 构成动作名词）
items.example: The motion passed by acclamation.
items.exampleCN: 动议以欢呼表决通过。

items.meaning: expressing acclamation
items.meaningCN: 表示欢呼的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The report noted the acclamatory tone of the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 报道注意到人群的欢呼语调。

items.meaning: praised widely
items.meaningCN: 广受赞誉的（-ed 分词形容词）
items.example: He is an acclaimed photographer.
items.exampleCN: 他是一位广受赞誉的摄影师。

items.meaning: not praised or recognised
items.meaningCN: 未获赞誉的；无人喝彩的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The unacclaimed play closed after a week.
items.exampleCN: 那部无人喝彩的戏一周后就停演了。

items.meaning: approval from reviewers
items.meaningCN: 评论界赞誉（文艺领域固定搭配）
items.example: The series earned critical acclaim but low ratings.
items.exampleCN: 这部剧获得评论界赞誉，但收视率低。

items.meaning: to gain public praise
items.meaningCN: 赢得赞誉（动词搭配）
items.example: The architect won acclaim for the museum.
items.exampleCN: 这位建筑师因博物馆赢得赞誉。

items.meaning: to be publicly praised as something
items.meaningCN: 被赞誉为……（被动搭配）
items.example: She was acclaimed as the finest voice of her generation.
items.exampleCN: 她被誉为她那一代最好的嗓音。

items.meaning: to praise a decision publicly
items.meaningCN: 公开称赞某项决定（动词搭配）
items.example: Business groups acclaimed the decision to cut the tax.
items.exampleCN: 商业团体称赞减税决定。

items.meaning: praise recognised across countries
items.meaningCN: 国际声誉（形容词搭配）
items.example: The film brought him international acclaim.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影为他带来国际声誉。

items.meaning: praise from the general public
items.meaningCN: 公众赞誉（形容词搭配）
items.example: The reform met with public acclaim.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革受到公众赞誉。

definition_zh: 住处；住宿；膳宿；调节；适应；和解、协议；（眼的）调节；（空间的）容纳能力；住房；语言趋同；（银行）通融、信贷
definition_en: a place to stay, the act of adjusting to fit, or an arrangement reached between parties
core_image: 一把椅子的靠背被调到刚好贴住人的脊背，不留缝也不顶人。
scene: We booked accommodation near the station for two nights.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 是「住处、住宿」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们在车站附近订了两晚住处。场景：拖着行李出站，抬头找旅馆招牌。

derivatives.zh: 容纳；为……提供住处；调节；适应

senses.title: Lodging or a place to stay
senses.titleCN: 住处：今晚有地方睡
senses.definition: a room, building, or other place where someone can stay temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 可供人临时住宿的房间、建筑或其他场所
senses.example: We booked accommodation near the station for two nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站附近订了两晚住处。
senses.why: The core verb means to fit something to a need. A room is accommodation because it is fitted to the traveller's need for shelter.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词意为“使适合需要”。房间之所以是 accommodation，是因为它被调适去满足旅人遮风避雨的需要。

senses.title: Adjustment to meet a need
senses.titleCN: 调节：把安排改到刚好合适
senses.definition: a change made so that something fits a person, a situation, or a requirement
senses.definitionCN: 为使某物适合某人、某种情况或某项要求而作出的改变
senses.example: The schedule needed a small accommodation for her disability.
senses.exampleCN: 日程需要为她的残障做一点调整。
senses.why: This is the verb's original shape: fitting one thing to another. The room sense is only one result of this act.
senses.whyCN: 这是动词最原本的形状：把一物调到与另一物相合。住宿义只是这个动作的一种结果。

senses.title: Settlement or agreement
senses.titleCN: 和解：双方各让一步，事就合上了
senses.definition: an arrangement or compromise reached between parties who differed
senses.definitionCN: 有分歧的各方之间达成的安排或妥协
senses.example: The two sides reached an accommodation on the border.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在边界问题上达成和解。
senses.why: Two positions must be fitted together until they no longer clash. A settlement is accommodation performed on interests rather than on furniture.
senses.whyCN: 两个立场必须被调到不再相撞为止。和解是对利益而非对家具做的 accommodation。

senses.title: Accommodation of the eye
senses.titleCN: 眼的调节：晶状体自己改焦距
senses.definition: in physiology, the adjustment of the lens of the eye to focus on objects at different distances
senses.definitionCN: 生理学中，眼晶状体为聚焦不同距离的物体而作的调整
senses.example: Reading at close range requires active accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 近距离阅读需要主动的调节。
senses.why: The eye physically changes shape to fit the distance. Physiology borrowed the everyday word for fitting because the lens literally accommodates.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛确实改变形状去适应距离。生理学借用这个日常词，是因为晶状体真的在“调适”。

senses.title: Space or capacity
senses.titleCN: 容纳：地方够不够装
senses.definition: the amount of space available to hold people or things
senses.definitionCN: 可容纳人或物的空间大小
senses.example: The hall has accommodation for five hundred guests.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅可容纳五百位客人。
senses.why: A container accommodates what fits inside it. Here the word measures the fit itself, not a room given to a guest.
senses.whyCN: 容器容纳装得进去的东西。这里的词量的是“装得下多少”，而不是给客人的那间房。

senses.title: Housing as a category
senses.titleCN: 住房：作为一类生活设施
senses.definition: housing considered as a collective need or provision, especially in policy
senses.definitionCN: 作为集体需求或供给来考虑的住房，尤用于政策语境
senses.example: The council promised more affordable accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会承诺提供更多可负担住房。
senses.why: Policy speaks of accommodation in the mass: not this room, but the stock of rooms a city must fit to its people.
senses.whyCN: 政策谈的是成批的 accommodation：不是这一间房，而是一座城市必须调适给其居民的全部住房。

senses.title: Linguistic accommodation
senses.titleCN: 语言趋同：说话人向对方靠
senses.definition: in sociolinguistics, the adjustment of speech style toward or away from the person one is talking to
senses.definitionCN: 社会语言学中，说话风格向交谈对象靠拢或远离的调整
senses.example: Her accent showed accommodation to the local dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 她的口音显示出对当地方言的趋同。
senses.why: Speech is fitted to the listener the way a key is fitted to a lock. The word's oldest move, adjusting one thing to another, is applied to voices.
senses.whyCN: 话语被调到听者身上，像钥匙被锉到锁里。这个词最古老的动作——把一物调到另一物——被用到了声音上。

senses.title: Banking accommodation
senses.titleCN: 通融：银行给你一段周转
senses.definition: in finance, a loan or credit facility granted as a favour or short-term support
senses.definitionCN: 金融中作为照顾或短期支持而给予的贷款或信贷便利
senses.example: The firm survived on a bank accommodation for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司靠银行通融撑了六个月。
senses.why: Here a creditor bends the usual terms to fit a borrower's difficulty. It is accommodation as flexibility rather than as lodging.
senses.whyCN: 这里是债权人把常规条款弯一弯，去适应借款人的困难。这是作为“灵活”的 accommodation，而非“住宿”。

intro.en: Accommodation comes from Latin accommodatio, from accommodare 'to fit to', built on commodus 'fitting'. Modus 'measure' is underneath, so the whole family is about things being measured to fit each other.
intro.cn: accommodation 来自拉丁语 accommodatio，源于 accommodare“使适合”，而后者建于 commodus“合适的”之上。再往下是 modus“尺度”，所以整个词族都与“量着调到相合”有关。

items.en: Measure, manner, limit. It gives mode, model, and modify, and it supplies the idea of a right amount.
items.cn: 尺度、方式、限度。它给出 mode、model、modify，并提供“恰当的分量”这一观念。

items.en: Fitting, convenient, suitable. Com- 'together' plus modus 'measure' means measured together, hence matching.
items.cn: 合适的、方便的、相宜的。com-“一起”加 modus“尺度”，意为“量在一起”，因而“相配”。

items.en: To fit to, adapt, make suitable. The prefix ad- 'to' assimilates to ac- before c, giving the doubled consonant.
items.cn: 使适合、适应、使相宜。前缀 ad-“向”在 c 前同化为 ac-，于是有了双写的辅音。

items.en: An adapting or fitting. The noun names the act, and Latin already used it for arranging things for a purpose.
items.cn: 调适、使相合。这个名词命名动作，拉丁语已用它指为某目的而安排事物。

items.en: French accommodation brings the word into English. Early English uses concern adjustment and agreement more than hotel rooms.
items.cn: 法语 accommodation 把这个词带入英语。早期英语用法多指调整与协议，而不是旅馆房间。

items.en: The lodging sense grows in the 17c, and later technical senses appear: the eye, sociolinguistics, and banking. The doubled c is fixed in spelling.
items.cn: 住宿义在 17 世纪发展起来，后来出现技术义：眼的调节、社会语言学、银行通融。双写 c 在拼写中固定下来。

note.en: The first group is the accommodation family plus a word from the same commodus root; the second separates a place to sleep from the act of adjusting and from a deal.
note.cn: 第一组是 accommodation 词族，外加一个同出 commodus 的词；第二组把“睡觉的地方”“调整的动作”与“谈成的协议”分开。

entries.definition: to provide room for, or to adjust to fit. It is the action that all the noun senses presuppose.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；为……提供住处；调节以适应；是名词各义项背后的动作。

entries.definition: willing to help or adjust to others. It describes a person, not a building.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于助人、愿意配合的；描述人，而非建筑。

entries.definition: relating to adjustment, especially of the eye or of policy. It is the neutral technical partner.
entries.definitionCN: 与调节相关的，尤指眼或政策；是中性的技术形容词。

entries.definition: roomy and convenient. It shares commodus but describes spaciousness, not the act of fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞方便的；共享 commodus，但描述空间大小，而非“调适”的动作。

entries.definition: a place to sleep, often temporary. It matches the first sense and carries no idea of adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 睡觉的地方，常为临时；对应第一义，不含“调整”之意。

entries.definition: buildings where people live, considered as a supply. It matches the policy sense of accommodation.
entries.definitionCN: 人们居住的建筑，作为供给来看；对应 accommodation 的政策义。

entries.definition: a small change made to improve a fit. It is the plain word for the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 为改善契合而作的小改动；是第二义的平实说法。

entries.definition: a change by which something becomes suited to new conditions. It is broader and more biological than accommodation.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物适应新条件的改变；比 accommodation 更宽泛，也更偏生物。

entries.definition: an official agreement ending a dispute. It matches the third sense and implies a formal close.
entries.definitionCN: 结束争端的正式协议；对应第三义，含正式收尾之意。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: com- 'together' plus modus 'measure' gives commodus 'fitting'; ad- 'to' gives accommodare 'to fit to'. The double c is assimilation.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：com-“一起”加 modus“尺度”得到 commodus“合适的”；ad-“向”得到 accommodare“使适合”。双写 c 是同化。

normal.en: Modus is measure: accommodation is measuring a thing until it fits.
normal.cn: modus 是尺度：accommodation 就是把某物量到刚好合适。

normal.en: A hotel room fits a traveller; a compromise fits two positions; the lens fits a distance.
normal.cn: 旅馆房间贴合旅人；妥协贴合两个立场；晶状体贴合距离。

normal.en: The doubled c is not a prefix; ad- simply became ac- before c.
normal.cn: 双写的 c 不是独立前缀；只是 ad- 在 c 前变成 ac-。

normal.en: British English says accommodation for a place to stay; American English often uses accommodations.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 accommodation 指住处；美式英语常用复数 accommodations。

normal.en: A bank accommodation bends the terms; a linguistic accommodation bends the accent.
normal.cn: 银行通融弯的是条款；语言趋同弯的是口音。

abstract.en: Accommodation is what two things do when neither can stay exactly as it was.
abstract.cn: 调适，是两样东西都不肯原样不动时所做的让步。

abstract.en: Every room is a theory about how much a person needs.
abstract.cn: 每一间房，都是一种关于“人需要多少”的理论。

abstract.en: To accommodate is to measure, and measuring always changes the thing measured.
abstract.cn: 调适就是量度，而量度总会改变被量之物。

examples.en: Student accommodation is scarce near the campus.
examples.cn: 校园附近的学生住宿很紧张。

examples.en: The design accommodates wheelchair users without a ramp.
examples.cn: 这个设计无需坡道也能容纳轮椅使用者。

examples.en: The union and the company reached an accommodation on hours.
examples.cn: 工会与公司在工时上达成和解。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，靠，没得事”——没订到酒店，靠朋友“调”出一间房 → accommodation 住宿、调节

root: 源自拉丁语 accommodare“使适合”，由 ad-“向”+ commodus“合适的”（com-“一起”+ modus“尺度”）构成；核心是“量着调到刚好相合”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accommodation, one act: fitting one thing to another. A room fits a guest, a schedule fits a need, a treaty fits two claims, a lens fits a distance, a voice fits a listener.
sensesIntro.cn: accommodation 的八个义项只有一个动作：把一物调到另一物上。房间贴客人，日程贴需要，协议贴两种主张，晶状体贴距离，口音贴听者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair back adjusted until it touches the spine without pressing.
core.cn: 核心意象：椅背被调到刚好贴住脊背，既不悬空也不顶人。

chain: ENGLISH: LODGING, AGREEMENT, AND TECHNICAL FITS

branches.en: SHELTER: one room fitted to one guest, or a city's stock of rooms fitted to its people.
branches.cn: 栖身：一间房调给一位客人，或一座城市的住房存量调给它的居民。

branches.en: FITTING: a schedule change and the eye's lens both alter a shape until it matches a demand.
branches.cn: 调适：日程改动与眼晶状体，都是改变形状直到与需求相合。

branches.en: AGREEMENT: two interests are measured against each other until they no longer collide.
branches.cn: 协议：两种利益被相互量度，直到不再相撞。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND CREDIT: a hall holds what fits inside it, and a bank bends terms to fit a borrower.
branches.cn: 容量与信贷：大厅装得下它内部容得下的，银行弯条款去贴合借款人。

branches.en: SPEECH: a speaker shifts accent toward the listener, fitting the voice to the ear.
branches.cn: 言语：说话人把口音移向听者，把声音调到耳朵上。

intro.en: Accommodation is a Latin -io noun. English builds the verb with -ate, the person adjective with -ing, the technical adjective with -ive, and uses the plural for lodging in American English.
intro.cn: accommodation 是拉丁语 -io 名词。英语用 -ate 造动词、-ing 造描述人的形容词、-ive 造技术形容词，并在美式英语中用复数指住宿。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is modus 'measure', commodus 'fitting', accommodare 'to fit to', and accommodatio 'an adapting'. The prefix ad- assimilates to ac- before c.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 modus“尺度”、commodus“合适的”、accommodare“使适合”、accommodatio“调适”。前缀 ad- 在 c 前同化为 ac-。

items.meaning: to provide room for, adapt to
items.meaningCN: 容纳；为……提供住处；适应（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The hall can accommodate 300 people.
items.exampleCN: 大厅可容纳三百人。

items.meaning: helpful, willing to adjust
items.meaningCN: 乐于助人的；随和的（-ing 构成形容词）
items.example: The staff were unusually accommodating.
items.exampleCN: 员工格外乐于助人。

items.meaning: relating to adjustment
items.meaningCN: 调节的；适应的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Accommodative monetary policy lowers rates.
items.exampleCN: 适应性货币政策会降低利率。

items.meaning: lodging, especially in American English
items.meaningCN: 住宿；膳宿（复数，尤用于美式英语）
items.example: The price includes meals and accommodations.
items.exampleCN: 价格含餐食与住宿。

items.meaning: rooms provided by a hotel
items.meaningCN: 酒店住宿（名词复合）
items.example: Hotel accommodation is included in the tour.
items.exampleCN: 行程含酒店住宿。

items.meaning: to adjust arrangements for someone
items.meaningCN: 作出调整；给予方便（动词搭配）
items.example: The school made accommodations for the exam.
items.exampleCN: 学校为考试作出了调整。

items.meaning: to arrive at a settlement
items.meaningCN: 达成和解（正式搭配）
items.example: The parties reached an accommodation after mediation.
items.exampleCN: 经调解，各方达成和解。

items.meaning: the lens's adjustment to focus
items.meaningCN: 眼的调节（生理学术语）
items.example: Age reduces the accommodation of the eye.
items.exampleCN: 年龄会降低眼的调节能力。

items.meaning: housing provided for living in
items.meaningCN: 居住用房（英式搭配）
items.example: The job comes with living accommodation.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作提供住宿。

items.meaning: a bill accepted as a favour without real consideration
items.meaningCN: 通融票据（为帮助他人而承兑的票据）
items.example: The accommodation bill was used to bridge a cash gap.
items.exampleCN: 这张通融票据用于填补现金缺口。

definition_zh: 积累；堆积；积聚物；财富的累积；资本积累；数据的累积；沉积（物）；体液潴留；（修辞）层层堆叠；累积而成的整体
definition_en: the gradual gathering of something into a mass, or the mass so gathered
core_image: 雪落在窗台上，一片一片，最后堆成一道高出窗沿的白脊。
scene: The slow accumulation of dust covered every shelf in the closed room.
sceneCN: 这里 accumulation 是「积累、堆积」（第 1 个义项）；句意：缓慢堆积的灰尘盖住了空房间里每一层架子。场景：多年没人进的书房，手指一抹就是一道痕。

senses.title: Gradual gathering into a mass
senses.titleCN: 积累：一点点攒成一堆
senses.definition: the process by which something increases in quantity by being added to over time
senses.definitionCN: 某物随时间不断被添加而数量增加的过程
senses.example: The slow accumulation of dust covered every shelf in the closed room.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢堆积的灰尘盖住了空房间里每一层架子。
senses.why: The Latin noun is a heaping up. Accumulation is not one arrival but many small arrivals that end as a single mass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词意为“堆起来”。accumulation 不是一次到达，而是许多次小到达最终成为一个整体。

senses.title: Buildup of wealth or possessions
senses.titleCN: 积攒：钱和东西越存越多
senses.definition: the gradual increase of money, goods, or property held by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体持有的金钱、货物或财产逐渐增加
senses.example: His accumulation of rare books began with a single purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 他的珍本收藏从一次购买开始。
senses.why: Objects added one by one become a collection. The physical heap turns into a portfolio, and the word follows it.
senses.whyCN: 一件件添入的物品成为收藏。物理的“堆”变成一份财产，词也跟着转过去。

senses.title: Increase of data or quantity
senses.titleCN: 累积：数字一层层加上去
senses.definition: the growth of a store of data, records, or measured values through repeated addition
senses.definitionCN: 数据、记录或测量值通过反复添加而增长
senses.example: The accumulation of sensor data soon exceeded the storage limit.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器数据的累积很快超出了存储上限。
senses.why: Modern data is a heap made of numbers. The same geometry as snow on a sill, only counted rather than weighed.
senses.whyCN: 现代数据是由数字堆成的堆。与窗台上的雪同一个几何，只是被计数而不是被称重。

senses.title: Capital accumulation
senses.titleCN: 资本积累：钱再投回去，越滚越大
senses.definition: in economics, the process of adding to capital stock by reinvesting surplus rather than consuming it
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中把剩余再投资而非消费、从而增加资本存量的过程
senses.example: Capital accumulation drove the industry's expansion.
senses.exampleCN: 资本积累推动了该产业的扩张。
senses.why: Economics gives the heap a direction: profit is not spent but stacked back into the productive base, so the pile compounds.
senses.whyCN: 经济学给这堆东西一个方向：利润不被花掉，而是叠回生产基础，于是越滚越大。

senses.title: Sediment accumulation
senses.titleCN: 沉积：泥沙一层层落下来
senses.definition: in geology, the deposition of sediment in layers over time
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中沉积物随时间一层层堆积
senses.example: Sediment accumulation at the river mouth formed a new delta.
senses.exampleCN: 河口的沉积作用形成了一片新三角洲。
senses.why: Geology reads time in layers. Each layer is a former heap, and the word names both the process and the record it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 地质学从层里读时间。每一层都是过去的一堆，这个词既命名过程，也命名它留下的记录。

senses.title: Fluid accumulation in the body
senses.titleCN: 潴留：水在身体里积住
senses.definition: in medicine, the abnormal collection of fluid in a tissue or cavity
senses.definitionCN: 医学中液体在组织或腔隙内的异常积聚
senses.example: Fluid accumulation in the lungs made breathing difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 肺部液体潴留让呼吸变得困难。
senses.why: Here the heap is unwelcome and internal. The neutral process becomes a symptom when what gathers cannot drain.
senses.whyCN: 这里的堆是不受欢迎的内在之物。当积聚的东西排不出去，中性的过程就成了症状。

senses.title: Rhetorical heaping of words
senses.titleCN: 层叠：词一句句往上码
senses.definition: in rhetoric, the piling up of words or phrases for emphasis, also called accumulatio
senses.definitionCN: 修辞学中为强调而把词语或短语层层堆叠，又称 accumulatio
senses.example: The speech ends in an accumulation of synonyms for betrayal.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲以一连串“背叛”的同义词收尾。
senses.why: Words can be heaped as things can. Rhetoric names the figure after the physical act, because emphasis is weight.
senses.whyCN: 词可以像东西一样堆。修辞学用这个物理动作来命名辞格，因为强调就是重量。

senses.title: The resulting mass
senses.titleCN: 积聚物：堆成之后的那个整体
senses.definition: the mass or store that results from a process of accumulation
senses.definitionCN: 积累过程结束后形成的堆积物或储备
senses.example: The accumulation in the attic turned out to be old letters.
senses.exampleCN: 阁楼里的那堆东西原来是旧信件。
senses.why: The noun can name either the act or its product. Here the verb has stopped, and what remains is a heap you can point at.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可命名动作，也可命名产物。这里动作已停，剩下的是可以用手指的一堆。

intro.en: Accumulation comes from Latin accumulatio, from accumulare 'to heap up', built on cumulus 'a heap'. English borrowed the noun in the 16c; the same cumulus names a heap-shaped cloud.
intro.cn: accumulation 来自拉丁语 accumulatio，源于 accumulare“堆起”，而后者建于 cumulus“堆”。英语 16 世纪借入该名词；同一个 cumulus 也命名堆状的积云。

items.en: A heap, a pile, a mass. It also gives the cloud name, because a cumulus cloud looks like a pile of cotton.
items.cn: 堆、垛、一团。它也是“积云”的名字来源，因为积云看起来就像一堆棉花。

items.en: To heap up, pile, or fill. The verb turns the shape into an action.
items.cn: 堆起、堆积、填满。这个动词把形状变成动作。

items.en: To, toward. Before c it assimilates to ac-, producing the doubled consonant in accumulare.
items.cn: 向、朝。在 c 前同化为 ac-，于是在 accumulare 中产生双写辅音。

items.en: To heap up, add to, amass. The prefix adds direction: the heap is built by adding toward an existing pile.
items.cn: 堆起、添加、积聚。前缀增加了方向：往已有的堆上添，才形成新的堆。

items.en: A heaping together. Rhetoric already used it for the piling of words, a sense English later revives.
items.cn: 堆在一起。修辞学已用它指词语的堆叠，这个义项英语后来重新拾起。

items.en: English takes the noun in the 16c. Later it is specialised in economics, geology, medicine, and data, each naming a different kind of heap.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个名词。后来它分别在经济、地质、医学与数据领域专业化，各自命名不同种类的堆。

note.en: The first group is the accumulation family, including the cloud word; the second distinguishes the process of heaping from the resulting store.
note.cn: 第一组是 accumulation 词族，含“云”那个词；第二组把“堆起来的过程”与“堆成之后的储备”分开。

entries.definition: to gather or grow into a mass over time. It is the process behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 积累、积聚；是名词背后的过程。

entries.definition: tending to accumulate. It describes a habit or tendency, not a finished total.
entries.definitionCN: 有积累倾向的；描述习性，而非已完成的总量。

entries.definition: increasing by successive additions. It focuses on the running total rather than the act of heaping.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步累加而增加的；重心在累计总量，而非“堆”的动作。

entries.definition: a heap-shaped cloud, or a heap in Latin. Same source, different domain: weather, not finance.
entries.definitionCN: 堆状的积云，或拉丁语中的“堆”。同源而不同领域：气象，而非金融。

entries.definition: a gradual increase or accumulation, often of pressure or evidence. It is the plain, often figurative word.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐增加或积聚，常指压力或证据；是平实、常带比喻的说法。

entries.definition: a group of things gathered together, often deliberately. It stresses selection rather than mere addition.
entries.definitionCN: 被聚在一起的一组东西，常为有意收集；强调挑选，而非单纯添加。

entries.definition: the gathering of a large amount, especially wealth or material. It is accumulation with an appetite.
entries.definitionCN: 大量聚敛，尤指财富或物资；是有胃口的 accumulation。

entries.definition: a large reserve kept for future use. It is the product sense, with a purpose attached.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来使用而储备的大量物资；是“产物”义，并带有目的。

entries.definition: growth by gradual external addition, as of layers or land. It is the geological cousin of accumulation.
entries.definitionCN: 靠外部逐渐添加而增长，如层或陆地；是 accumulation 的地质表亲。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: cumulus 'heap' plus ad- 'to' gives accumulare 'to heap up'. The double c is assimilation, and cumulus also names the cloud.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：cumulus“堆”加 ad-“向”得到 accumulare“堆起”。双写 c 是同化，cumulus 也是“积云”的名字。

normal.en: Cumulus is a heap: accumulation is the heap forming, not the heap already formed.
normal.cn: cumulus 是堆：accumulation 是堆正在形成，而不是堆已经形成。

normal.en: Dust, money, data, and sediment all obey the same rule: add small amounts for a long time.
normal.cn: 灰尘、金钱、数据、泥沙都遵守同一条规则：少量，长时间，不断添加。

normal.en: Cumulus also names the cloud, because a cloud can look like a pile of cotton.
normal.cn: cumulus 也是云的名字，因为云可以看起来像一堆棉花。

normal.en: Capital accumulation is a heap that is reinvested instead of spent.
normal.cn: 资本积累是一堆不拿去花、而是再投回去的堆。

normal.en: Fluid accumulation is the same heap when it cannot drain.
normal.cn: 液体潴留就是同一堆东西排不出去的时候。

abstract.en: Accumulation hides its own history: you only see the pile, never the adding.
abstract.cn: 积累藏起了自己的历史：你只看见堆，看不见一次次添加。

abstract.en: Time is the only ingredient every accumulation shares.
abstract.cn: 时间是每一种积累都共享的唯一配料。

abstract.en: What gathers slowly can also be dispersed slowly.
abstract.cn: 慢慢聚起的东西，也会慢慢散掉。

examples.en: The accumulation of snow closed the mountain pass.
examples.cn: 积雪封住了山口。

examples.en: Years of accumulation of evidence finally made the case clear.
examples.cn: 多年证据的累积终于让案情清晰。

examples.en: The museum's accumulation of drawings fills twelve rooms.
examples.cn: 博物馆收藏的素描塞满了十二个展厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，Q 米，来神”——米粒一颗颗往 Q 里堆，越堆越高 → accumulation 积累、堆积

root: 源自拉丁语 accumulare“堆起”，由 ad-“向”+ cumulus“堆”构成，名词 accumulatio 加 -io；核心是“少量反复添加，最终成一堆”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accumulation, one geometry: many small additions become one heap. The heap can be dust, money, data, capital, sediment, fluid, words, or the pile left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: accumulation 的八个义项只有一个几何：许多次小的添加变成一个堆。这个堆可以是灰尘、金钱、数据、资本、泥沙、体液、词语，或堆完剩下的那一坨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: snow landing flake by flake until it stands above the window ledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：雪一片一片落下，最后高出窗台。

chain: AD- + CUMULARE = ACCUMULARE, TO HEAP TO
SPECIALISED HEAPS: WEALTH, DATA, CAPITAL, SEDIMENT, FLUID, WORDS

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: the slow adding and the mass it leaves are the same noun seen before and after it stops.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：缓慢添加与它留下的堆，是同一个名词在停下之前与停下之后。

branches.en: WEALTH: a private collection and an economy's reinvested capital are heaps with an owner.
branches.cn: 财富：私人收藏与经济中再投资的资本，都是有主人的堆。

branches.en: DATA: numbers added one reading at a time become a store that can overflow its disk.
branches.cn: 数据：一次一个读数加起来的数字，成为可能撑爆磁盘的储备。

branches.en: NATURE: sediment builds a delta, and fluid builds a symptom; one is welcome, one is not.
branches.cn: 自然：泥沙堆出三角洲，液体堆出症状；一个受欢迎，一个不受欢迎。

branches.en: RHETORIC: words are piled until the sentence carries weight.
branches.cn: 修辞：词语被堆起来，直到句子有了重量。

intro.en: Accumulation is a Latin -io noun. English forms the verb with -ate, the tendency adjective with -ive, the possibility adjective with -able, and keeps cumulative from the same root.
intro.cn: accumulation 是拉丁语 -io 名词。英语用 -ate 造动词、-ive 造倾向形容词、-able 造可能性形容词，并保留同根的 cumulative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is cumulus 'heap', cumulare 'to heap', accumulare 'to heap up', and accumulatio 'a heaping'. The prefix ad- assimilates to ac- before c.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 cumulus“堆”、cumulare“堆”、accumulare“堆起”、accumulatio“堆聚”。前缀 ad- 在 c 前同化为 ac-。

items.meaning: to gather or grow into a mass
items.meaningCN: 积累；积聚（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Interest accumulates over the year.
items.exampleCN: 利息在一年中累积。

items.meaning: tending to accumulate
items.meaningCN: 累积性的；有积累倾向的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The process has an accumulative effect.
items.exampleCN: 这一过程有累积效应。

items.meaning: able to be accumulated
items.meaningCN: 可积累的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: Only accumulable goods can be stored.
items.exampleCN: 只有可积累的货物才能储存。

items.meaning: increasing by successive additions
items.meaningCN: 累积的；渐增的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The cumulative effect of small errors is large.
items.exampleCN: 小错误的累积效应很大。

items.meaning: the gradual growth of personal wealth
items.meaningCN: 财富的积累（名词搭配）
items.example: Tax policy affects the accumulation of wealth.
items.exampleCN: 税收政策影响财富积累。

items.meaning: the growing store of recorded information
items.meaningCN: 数据的累积（名词搭配）
items.example: The accumulation of data made the pattern visible.
items.exampleCN: 数据的累积让规律显现。

items.meaning: growth of capital by reinvestment
items.meaningCN: 资本积累（经济学术语）
items.example: Capital accumulation requires saving, not spending.
items.exampleCN: 资本积累需要储蓄而非消费。

items.meaning: the building of sedimentary layers
items.meaningCN: 沉积物堆积（地质学术语）
items.example: Sediment accumulation raised the riverbed.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物堆积抬高了河床。

items.meaning: abnormal collection of fluid in tissue
items.meaningCN: 体液潴留（医学术语）
items.example: Fluid accumulation can signal heart failure.
items.exampleCN: 体液潴留可能是心力衰竭的信号。

items.meaning: the gradual building of a case
items.meaningCN: 证据的累积（法律搭配）
items.example: The accumulation of evidence took three years.
items.exampleCN: 证据的累积花了三年。

definition_zh: 准确；精确；准确度；正确性；（测量的）准确度；命中精度；事实上的真实性；（统计）与真值的接近程度；仪器的精密度；复制的保真度；预测的准确率；语法正确性
definition_en: the quality of being correct or exact, especially in measurement, fact, or aim
core_image: 一支箭落在靶心，箭杆与圆心连成一条直线。
scene: The clock's accuracy was tested against an atomic standard.
sceneCN: 这里 accuracy 是「仪器的精密度、准确度」（第 5 个义项）；句意：这只钟的准确度是拿原子钟标准来检验的。场景：实验室里两只时间显示并排，差值被逐日记录。

derivatives.zh: 准确的；精确的；正确无误的

senses.title: Correctness of measurement
senses.titleCN: 准确度：量出来的数离真值多近
senses.definition: the degree to which a measurement agrees with the true value of what is measured
senses.definitionCN: 测量结果与被测量真值的一致程度
senses.example: The accuracy of the survey depends on the calibration of the instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 测量的准确度取决于仪器的校准。
senses.why: Latin accuratus means done with care. Accuracy is the visible result of that care: a number that lands where it should.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accuratus 意为“用心做的”。accuracy 是这份用心的可见结果：一个落在应在位置上的数。

senses.title: Accuracy of aim
senses.titleCN: 准头：出手就中
senses.definition: the quality of hitting the intended target, as in shooting, throwing, or passing
senses.definitionCN: 击中预定目标的品质，如射击、投掷或传球
senses.example: The archer's accuracy improved with every round.
senses.exampleCN: 弓箭手的准头一轮比一轮好。
senses.why: The target gives accuracy a visible centre. What counts is not effort but the distance between the arrow and the mark.
senses.whyCN: 靶子给了 accuracy 一个看得见的中心。算数的不是努力，而是箭与标记之间的距离。

senses.title: Factual truthfulness
senses.titleCN: 属实：说的与发生的一致
senses.definition: the quality of a statement or account being true to the facts
senses.definitionCN: 陈述或叙述与事实相符的品质
senses.example: The report's accuracy was questioned by two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 两名目击者质疑这份报告的准确性。
senses.why: Facts are the target of a sentence. To speak with accuracy is to hit what happened rather than what one wishes had happened.
senses.whyCN: 事实就是句子的靶心。说得准确，就是击中所发生的事，而不是希望发生的事。

senses.title: Statistical closeness to a true value
senses.titleCN: 统计准确度：估计值偏不偏
senses.definition: in statistics, the closeness of a measured or estimated value to the true value, as opposed to mere consistency
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中测量值或估计值与真值的接近程度，区别于单纯的稳定性
senses.example: The model's accuracy fell when the sample was small.
senses.exampleCN: 样本变小时，模型的准确度下降了。
senses.why: Statistics separates accuracy from precision: one is closeness to the centre, the other is tightness of the cluster. This sense names the first.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把准确度与精密度分开：一个离中心多近，一个是点簇多紧。这个义项命名前者。

senses.title: Precision of a device
senses.titleCN: 精密度：仪器读数稳不稳、准不准
senses.definition: the ability of an instrument to give readings close to the true value consistently
senses.definitionCN: 仪器能稳定给出接近真值读数的能力
senses.example: The clock's accuracy was tested against an atomic standard.
senses.exampleCN: 这只钟的准确度是拿原子钟标准来检验的。
senses.why: A device is accurate when its readings can be trusted as close to the truth. The word shifts from the result to the property of the machine that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器的读数可以被信赖为接近真值，它就是 accurate。这个词从结果转到了产生结果的机器属性上。

senses.title: Fidelity of reproduction
senses.titleCN: 保真：复制出来的还像原件
senses.definition: the degree to which a copy, recording, or translation preserves the original
senses.definitionCN: 复制品、录音或译文保留原物的程度
senses.example: The accuracy of the recording surprised the engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 录音的保真度让工程师们吃惊。
senses.why: Here the target is the original itself. Accuracy measures how little the copy has drifted from its source.
senses.whyCN: 这里的靶心是原件本身。accuracy 量的是复制品偏离源头有多少。

senses.title: Predictive accuracy
senses.titleCN: 预测准确率：说中了多少
senses.definition: the proportion of predictions that turn out correct, used in forecasting and machine learning
senses.definitionCN: 预测结果正确的比例，用于预报与机器学习
senses.example: The forecast's accuracy dropped sharply after the storm changed course.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴改道后，预报的准确率骤降。
senses.why: A prediction aims at a future that has not happened yet. Accuracy is scored after the fact, when the arrow either lands or does not.
senses.whyCN: 预测瞄准的是尚未发生的未来。准确率是事后打的分，那时箭要么中了，要么没中。

senses.title: Grammatical accuracy
senses.titleCN: 语法正确：句子合乎规则
senses.definition: in language learning and assessment, correctness in grammar, spelling, and usage
senses.definitionCN: 语言学习与评估中，语法、拼写与用法的正确性
senses.example: The test scores fluency and accuracy separately.
senses.exampleCN: 这项考试把流利度与准确度分开计分。
senses.why: A grammar is a set of rules, and a sentence either follows them or does not. Accuracy here is conformity to a written target rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 语法是一套规则，句子要么遵守，要么不遵守。这里的 accuracy 是对书面靶心的符合，而非物理靶心。

intro.en: Accuracy is built on the English adjective accurate, which comes from Latin accuratus 'carefully done', from accurare 'to take care of'. The noun with -cy was formed in English, not inherited from a classical Latin noun.
intro.cn: accuracy 建于英语形容词 accurate 之上，而 accurate 来自拉丁语 accuratus“用心做的”，源于 accurare“照料、用心处理”。带 -cy 的名词是在英语中构成的，并非直接承自古典拉丁名词。

items.en: Care, attention, concern. It gives cure, curious, and accurate, and it is the moral core of the whole family.
items.cn: 关心、注意、挂念。它给出 cure、curious、accurate，是整个词族的道德核心。

items.en: To take care of, to do with care, to prepare carefully. The prefix ad- adds direction: care applied to a task.
items.cn: 照料、用心做、仔细准备。前缀 ad- 增加方向：把关心施加到某项任务上。

items.en: The past participle means carefully done, exact, precise. Latin used it of work and of speech.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为“用心完成的、精确的、准确的”。拉丁语用它形容工作与言辞。

items.en: English borrows the adjective in the 17c. It first describes careful work, then, with the rise of measurement, exact numbers.
items.cn: 英语 17 世纪借入这个形容词。它先形容用心的成果，随着测量兴起，再形容精确的数字。

items.en: The noun is formed in English with -cy on the model of other abstract nouns. There is no classical Latin accuratia, so this is an English coinage from a Latin base.
items.cn: 这个名词是英语仿其他抽象名词用 -cy 构成的。古典拉丁语没有 accuratia，因此它是以拉丁词基在英语中造出的词。

items.en: Metrology, statistics, computing, and language testing each give accuracy a formal definition. The -cy noun becomes the standard abstract label in all of them.
items.cn: 计量学、统计学、计算与语言测试各自给 accuracy 一个正式定义。这个 -cy 名词在所有这些领域都成了标准的抽象标签。

note.en: The first group is the accurate family; the second separates accuracy from precision, which statistics treats as a different virtue.
note.cn: 第一组是 accurate 词族；第二组把 accuracy 与 precision 分开，统计学把二者当作不同的德性。

entries.definition: correct and exact. It describes the result, while accuracy names the quality.
entries.definitionCN: 准确、精确的；描述结果，而 accuracy 命名性质。
